processes.name: Goal setting & check-ins
processes.summary: Sets cascaded company, team and individual goals each half-year and keeps a documented rhythm of check-ins in the Darwinbox performance module, so year-end reviews rest on dated evidence rather than recall. Covers all regular employees globally; interns and fixed-term staff use a lighter version. Good looks like 3-5 measurable goals per person approved within 30 days of cycle start, quarterly check-ins for at least 85% of employees, and no surprises at review time.
processes.trigger: Executive OKRs approved for the half (January and July), a new hire's start date, or an internal job change
outputs: Approved individual goals in the Performance module (Darwinbox)
Documented check-in notes (monthly 1:1s, at least quarterly)
Goal revisions with reason and audit trail
Goal-setting and check-in completion dashboard by org
Job-family goal guidance (engineering OKRs, sales quota linkage)
processes.sla: Goals approved within 30 calendar days of cycle start or hire/transfer; check-ins at least quarterly

steps.label: Open goal cycle in Darwinbox
steps.detail: Publish approved company and org OKRs in the Performance module, set cycle dates and eligibility (hires after the cut-off get a pro-rated cycle) and send manager guidance with good and bad goal examples by job family.

steps.label: Cascade team objectives
steps.detail: Run a team session translating org OKRs into 3-5 team objectives. Engineering objectives should reference outcomes such as tape-out readiness, verification coverage or silicon bring-up milestones, not activity counts.

steps.label: Draft 3-5 individual goals
steps.detail: Draft SMART goals linked to a team objective, with weights, plus one development goal. Sales roles reference the CO-04 quota plan instead of restating it.

steps.label: Review and approve goals
steps.detail: Check measurability, weighting and consistency with peers at the same level; approve in Darwinbox or return with comments. Reject goals that depend on unrecorded overtime for non-exempt staff or on attendance metrics.
steps.control: Goals count toward the review only after manager approval; edits are logged.

steps.label: Goals approved within 30 days?
steps.detail: HRBP reviews the completion dashboard by org at day 30 and flags managers with missing or unapproved goals.

steps.label: Escalate overdue goal setting
steps.detail: Send reminders to the manager, then escalate to the Dept Head with a list of employees without approved goals; set a 10-day catch-up date.

steps.label: Hold documented check-ins
steps.detail: Monthly 1:1s with at least a quarterly check-in recorded in Darwinbox: progress, blockers, feedback given and support offered. Notes should be dated, factual and job-related because they become evidence in PD-02 and PD-03.

steps.label: Update progress and request changes
steps.detail: Employee updates goal status before each check-in. Material changes (re-prioritized project, re-org, extended leave) go through the goal-change workflow so the record shows why the target moved.

steps.label: Report completion and quality
steps.detail: Publish a monthly dashboard of goal approval and check-in completion by org; HRBPs sample 10 goals per org each half for quality and flag orgs under 85% before mid-year.

steps.label: Lock goals and feed review
steps.detail: At cycle end, goals and check-in notes lock and flow into the PD-02 review form; late changes need HRBP approval.

raci.activity: Company/org OKR publication and cycle setup

controls.control: Goal approval workflow: goals count toward the review only after manager approval; changes after approval are logged with reason
Monthly check-in compliance review; orgs below 85% quarterly check-in completion escalated to Dept Head
AI goal-suggestion or productivity-scoring features enabled only after DS-06 review; no automated ratings derived from goal data

kpis.name: Goals approved within 30 days
kpis.why: Late goals mean reviews are judged against targets set after the fact.

kpis.name: Quarterly check-in completion
kpis.why: Documented check-ins are the evidence base for fair ratings and any later PIP.

kpis.name: 'I know what is expected of me' (engagement item)
kpis.why: Tests whether goals are actually understood, not just entered.

considerations: Keep goals few and outcome-based; a 12-goal list shows no prioritization and is useless in calibration.
Do not duplicate the sales quota in the performance form; reference the CO-04 plan so payout and rating signals cannot conflict.
Check-in notes are discoverable and in California are part of the personnel file; write observations, never speculation about health, family or immigration status.
Adjust or pro-rate goals for protected leave instead of scoring against a full-year target (FMLA/CFRA, Taiwan sick-leave protection, Canada statutory leaves).
Chip schedules slip for reasons outside an individual's control (foundry capacity, silicon bugs); score contribution and quality of work, not only milestone dates.

variations.when: New hire or internal transfer mid-cycle
variations.how: Goals set within 30 days of start or transfer with pro-rated weights; the ON-04 30/60/90 plan can serve as the first-cycle goals.
The CO-04 quota and territory plan is the primary goal; add 1-2 non-quota goals such as account planning and export/anti-bribery compliance.
Pause the cycle; reset goals within 30 days of return (LV-03) and exclude the leave period from assessment.

countries.us: No statutory goal-setting rules; keep goals job-related and remember NLRA Section 7 protects non-supervisory employees who discuss goals, workload or pay. AI tools that score goals or productivity for IL, CO or NYC staff can trigger notice duties (IL HB 3773 from Jan 2026; CO SB 26-189 from Jan 2027).
countries.us-ca: Goal and check-in records are part of the personnel file employees can inspect within 30 days (LC 1198.5). Never set goals that require non-exempt staff to work off the clock or skip meal and rest breaks.
countries.ca: No statutory rules, but clear, acknowledged expectations are the starting point for any later performance-management or cause argument (McKinley v. BC Tel). Ontario employers with 25+ employees must disclose in the electronic monitoring policy any system telemetry used to track goals.
countries.in: No statutory process; many individual-contributor engineers are 'workers' under the Labour Codes, so written goals and dated check-ins are the basis for any later performance action. Karnataka IT establishments using the standing-orders exemption should route goal-related grievances through the GRC.
countries.tw: Courts reviewing an LSA Art. 11(5) incompetence dismissal look for objective standards communicated in advance, so issue goals in writing (bilingual, Chinese prevailing). From 2026 up to 10 days of sick leave a year cannot lower appraisals, so keep attendance out of goals.
countries.cn: Objective, communicated standards are a precondition for an LCL Art. 40(2) incompetence process; have employees e-confirm goals and keep the record. Performance rules that affect pay or discipline must go through democratic procedure and be publicized (LCL Art. 4).

processes.name: Performance review & calibration
processes.summary: Runs the annual (optionally semiannual) review cycle in the Darwinbox performance module: self, manager and peer input, calibration against guidance distributions, bias and leave-protection checks, locked ratings that feed the annual compensation review (CO-02) and bonus (CO-03), and documented review conversations. Applies to all regular employees in the US, Canada, India, Taiwan and China, with local overlays for leave, language and termination-evidence rules. Good looks like on-time completion, calibrated and explainable ratings with no unexplained adverse impact, and every employee receiving a written review they have acknowledged.
processes.owner: HRBP (process and calibration), People Ops (cycle administration), Dept Heads (rating approval), Legal/Employee Relations (high-risk review)
processes.trigger: Annual review calendar (fiscal year-end; optional mid-year cycle) opened by People Ops after PD-01 goals close
outputs: Self, peer and manager reviews in the Performance module (Darwinbox)
Calibrated, locked ratings with calibration notes
Adverse-impact and leave-status analytics pack
Ratings file reconciled into the comp planning tool for CO-02/CO-03
Employee-acknowledged written reviews (local language where needed)
Appeal and PIP referral log
processes.sla: 8-10 weeks from launch to conversations: self/peer 2 weeks, drafts 2 weeks, calibration 3 weeks, conversations within 3 weeks of lock

steps.label: Launch review cycle in Darwinbox
steps.detail: Configure forms, 5-point scale, eligibility cut-off (e.g., hired after 1 Oct = not rated), rater assignments and languages (English, Traditional and Simplified Chinese). Import goals and check-ins from PD-01 and flag employees on leave or with pending accommodations for special handling.

steps.label: Complete self-assessment
steps.detail: Summarize results against goals with evidence, behaviors and development needs. Employees on leave may submit on return; their deadline pauses.

steps.label: Request peer feedback
steps.detail: Select 3-5 peers including cross-functional partners (e.g., physical design for an RTL engineer). Peer input informs the manager, is summarized to the employee and is never a vote.

steps.label: Draft review and proposed rating
steps.detail: Write an evidence-based review citing dated examples from check-ins. AI drafting is allowed only in approved tools under POL-50: the manager edits and owns the text and decides the rating, and no health, leave or peer-identifying data is pasted into prompts. Rate only on time worked; exclude protected leave periods.
steps.control: Form requires manager attestation that the rating is a human decision and any AI draft was reviewed.

steps.label: Run pre-calibration bias analytics
steps.detail: Produce distributions by org, level, gender, age 40+, race/ethnicity (US, where lawfully held), leave status, visa status, location and part-time status, with four-fifths flags and deviations from guidance. Use aggregated, de-identified views for China and India under local privacy rules.

steps.label: Facilitate calibration sessions
steps.detail: Dept Head, managers and HRBP calibrate bottom ratings first, then top ratings, against written level criteria. Guidance distribution (e.g., 15-20% top two ratings, 5-10% below expectations) is not forced; deviations need a written rationale. HRBP runs bias interrupters and records factual notes.

steps.label: Ratings consistent and supported?
steps.detail: Dept Head confirms each rating is supported by evidence and consistent across teams and groups.

steps.label: Revise rating or add evidence
steps.detail: Manager adds dated evidence or adjusts the rating; changes return to the next calibration session.

steps.label: Review high-risk ratings
steps.detail: Employment counsel and Employee Relations review below-expectations ratings for employees with protected activity in the last 12 months (CA: 90-day presumption), on or recently back from protected leave, with pending accommodations, or in China/Taiwan where the rating may support an incompetence process.
steps.control: No below-expectations rating in the high-risk population is released without ER/Legal sign-off.

steps.label: Approve and lock final ratings
steps.detail: Dept Head approves; People Ops locks ratings in Darwinbox and transfers them to the comp planning tool for CO-02/CO-03 with a record-count reconciliation. Post-lock changes need HRBP and Dept Head approval with a reason.
steps.control: Rating lock and reconciliation to comp planning (ratings drive bonus accruals reviewed under SOX).

steps.label: Hold review conversation
steps.detail: Deliver the written review in a 1:1 (video for remote staff) within 3 weeks of lock, in the employee's working language; focus on evidence and development. HRBP preps managers for below-expectations conversations. Pay letters follow via CO-02.

steps.label: Acknowledge and add comments
steps.detail: Employee e-acknowledges receipt (not agreement) in Darwinbox and may add comments within 10 business days. In China and Taiwan the acknowledgment is key evidence; if the employee refuses, the manager records delivery with a witness.

steps.label: Appeal or below expectations?
steps.detail: HRBP checks for a formal appeal and for below-expectations ratings that need follow-up.

steps.label: Resolve appeal within 30 days
steps.detail: Skip-level manager and HRBP review the evidence and calibration notes, meet the employee and issue a written outcome; ER takes over if the appeal alleges discrimination or retaliation (ER-01).

steps.label: Route to coaching or PIP
steps.detail: Agree next steps with the manager: documented coaching for first-time low ratings, or PD-03 PIP after ER screening. Never launch a PIP in the same meeting as the review.

steps.label: Close cycle and archive records
steps.detail: Archive reviews, calibration notes and analytics under the retention schedule (CA: 4 years for ADS data; CN: at least 2 years after contract end) and publish cycle metrics.

raci.activity: Cycle design, forms and rating scale

controls.control: Pre-calibration adverse-impact analysis (four-fifths flags) by protected group, leave status and visa status, reviewed before ratings lock
Rating lock after Dept Head approval; post-lock changes require HRBP + Dept Head approval with reason
ER/Legal review of below-expectations ratings for employees with recent protected activity, protected leave or pending accommodation
controls.evidence: ER review log in case management

controls.control: Leave-protection check: no rating based on FMLA/CFRA/statutory leave or on up to 10 Taiwan sick days
AI drafting governance: approved tools only, manager attestation of human decision, no sensitive data in prompts
controls.evidence: POL-50 attestation field; DS-06 tool approval

controls.control: Record-count and rating reconciliation between Darwinbox and the comp planning tool

kpis.name: Reviews completed by deadline
kpis.why: Late reviews delay pay decisions and weaken the evidence trail.

kpis.name: Calibration coverage
kpis.why: Uncalibrated orgs drift into rating inflation or harshness.

kpis.name: Unexplained adverse impact in final ratings
kpis.target: 0 groups below four-fifths without documented review
kpis.why: Ratings drive pay, promotion and RIF selection; disparities are litigation exhibits.

kpis.name: Review conversations held within 3 weeks of lock
kpis.why: Unexplained ratings drive disengagement and appeals.

kpis.name: Appeals filed / upheld
kpis.why: A spike signals unclear criteria or poor calibration.

kpis.name: 'My review was fair' (post-cycle pulse)
kpis.why: Perceived fairness predicts retention of engineers.

considerations: Use a guidance distribution, not forced ranking: forced curves in teams under about 25 people create arbitrary low ratings and exhibits for plaintiffs; allow deviation with written rationale.
Calibrate the bottom first and require dated evidence from check-ins for every below-expectations rating; these ratings feed PD-03 and RIF selection and carry the most legal risk.
Deliver the rating and development conversation before or separately from the pay letter where the calendar allows; bundling turns the conversation into a pay negotiation.
Employees who worked less than about 3 months of the cycle because of leave should be 'not rated' with bonus handled under the plan, not defaulted to 'meets' or penalized.

AI-drafted reviews: CRD ADS regulations treat algorithmic tools used in promotion or pay decisions as within FEHA, and CCPA ADMT duties start 1 Jan 2027; keep humans deciding, keep inputs and outputs for 4 years in CA, and never let tools infer ratings from telemetry.
Engineering peer feedback over-rewards visible work (architecture, customer escalations) and under-rewards verification, DFT and infrastructure; calibrate across job families with level criteria.
Ratings feed RIF selection and visa-heavy teams draw scrutiny for national-origin and citizenship bias (EEOC, DOJ IER, DOL Project Firewall); include visa status in the adverse-impact check.
In China and Taiwan a below-expectations rating is the first exhibit in an incompetence dismissal; objective criteria, translation and acknowledgment matter more than narrative quality.
Calibration notes are discoverable: record evidence and decisions, never comments about age, family plans, accent, health or 'culture fit'.

variations.how: Mid-year uses a lighter check (no rating or a provisional rating, no calibration below Director level); the annual cycle carries the formal rating that feeds CO-02.
Not rated; manager gives written onboarding feedback; bonus pro-rated under CO-03 plan rules.

variations.when: Employee on leave at cycle time
variations.how: Rate on the period worked (or 'not rated'); defer the conversation until return (LV-03); HRBP sensitivity review before lock.
Quota attainment from CO-04 informs but does not mechanically set the rating; compliance behaviors (export screening, gifts) are rated explicitly.
CEO rates the executive team and presents to the Comp Committee under CO-07; the Board evaluates the CEO.

variations.when: Employee on a PIP or under investigation
variations.how: Rate normally with ER input; do not wait for the PIP or investigation to end, and do not reference unproven allegations.
Changes to the scale or its pay consequences go through democratic procedure and are publicized before use (LCL Art. 4).

countries.us: At-will employment does not reduce risk here: ratings are the main evidence in discrimination and retaliation claims, and Muldrow v. St. Louis (2024) lowered the harm threshold for job-change claims, so review calibration outcomes for adverse impact. FMLA leave cannot be counted against the employee in ratings (29 CFR 825.220(c)); rate on time worked. Automated performance tools can trigger IL HB 3773 notice duties (from Jan 2026) and CO SB 26-189 duties (from Jan 2027), and NYC LL 144 bias audits apply to tools that screen NYC promotion candidates.
countries.us-ca: CRD ADS regulations (effective 1 Oct 2025) make discriminatory outcomes from AI or algorithmic tools used in promotion and pay decisions FEHA violations, including through vendors; keep a human decision-maker and ADS records for 4 years, and prepare for CCPA ADMT notice and opt-out/appeal duties from 1 Jan 2027. CFRA and PDL leave cannot be held against the employee, and adverse action (including a low rating that cuts pay or leads to a PIP) within 90 days of wage, whistleblower or equal-pay protected activity carries a rebuttable presumption of retaliation (LC 98.6, 1102.5). Reviews are part of the personnel file producible within 30 days (LC 1198.5).
countries.ca: There is no at-will employment, so a documented, acknowledged review history is the foundation of any later performance-management or cause argument, which requires clear expectations, warnings and a real chance to improve (McKinley). Seniority and service keep accruing during statutory leaves in Ontario and BC, and a low rating linked to leave, disability or family status invites human rights complaints (1-year limit at the HRTO and BC Tribunal). Ontario's electronic monitoring policy must disclose any electronic data used in ratings.
countries.in: There is no statutory appraisal process; many Bengaluru GCCs run appraisals on the April-March financial year, so if the global cycle is calendar-based, communicate increment timing clearly (market practice). For 'workers' (many individual-contributor engineers), a poor rating later used to support dismissal must survive natural-justice scrutiny, so ratings must be evidence-based and communicated. Rating-linked pay outcomes must not differ by gender for the same or similar work (Code on Wages s.3).
countries.tw: From 1 Jan 2026, taking up to 10 days of sick leave a year cannot lead to adverse appraisal, promotion or transfer outcomes (Regulations of Leave-Taking by Workers Art. 9-1), and pregnancy, parental leave or complaints cannot be penalized. Ratings are a core exhibit in any LSA Art. 11(5) dismissal, where courts expect objective standards, coaching and consideration of reassignment. Deliver reviews in Traditional Chinese or bilingual form and keep the acknowledgment.
countries.cn: An LCL Art. 40(2) incompetence process requires objective, communicated standards and evidence of failure, so the rating scale, criteria and consequences should be adopted through democratic procedure, publicized (LCL Art. 4) and each review acknowledged in writing. Employees in Art. 42 protected categories (pregnancy, medical treatment period, pending occupational-disease exam) should not face rating-driven adverse action. Transferring review data to US systems needs a PIPL notice and separate consent for cross-border transfer unless the HR-management exemption genuinely applies.

processes.name: Performance improvement plan
processes.summary: A structured, time-boxed plan (30, 60 or 90 days) to close a documented performance gap after coaching has failed, with ER/Legal risk screening before issue, SMART goals, real support, weekly documented check-ins and a defined outcome (success, extension, reassignment or exit). Global process with mandatory country overlays: China's Art. 40(2) training-or-adjustment sequence, Taiwan's last-resort principle, India's natural-justice expectations and Canada's without-cause economics. Good looks like PIPs that genuinely rescue a meaningful share of employees and, where they do not, an exit that is defensible in the relevant forum.
processes.owner: HRBP (process), Employee Relations (risk and quality), Legal (non-US and high-risk sign-off), Manager (execution)
processes.trigger: Below-expectations rating (PD-02) or a sustained, documented gap after at least 30 days of informal coaching
outputs: ER risk screen record
Signed/acknowledged PIP document (T-PIP, local language)
Weekly check-in summaries
Training or job-adjustment record (mandatory in China)
Written outcome letter (close, extend, reassign or exit)
Hand-off file to OF-02/OF-04 where applicable
processes.sla: ER screen within 5 business days of request; PIP of 30/60/90 days; outcome decision within 5 business days of PIP end

steps.label: Identify sustained performance gap
steps.detail: Manager brings dated evidence (missed deliverables, quality metrics, check-in notes) to the HRBP. Conduct issues go to ER-04 corrective action, not a PIP.

steps.label: Document pre-PIP coaching
steps.detail: At least 30 days of documented coaching with clear expectations and offered support, confirmed in follow-up emails, unless the gap is severe and already documented in PD-02.

steps.label: Run ER risk screen
steps.detail: Check protected activity in the last 12 months (complaints, whistleblowing, wage claims, concerted activity), leave taken or requested, accommodation or pregnancy disclosures, age 40+ comparators, visa status, recent transfers and prior ratings. Flag the CA 90-day retaliation presumption.
steps.control: No PIP is issued without a completed ER screen.

steps.label: Proceed with PIP?
steps.detail: Employment counsel decides on the screen outcome (mandatory for all non-US PIPs and high-risk US cases).

steps.label: Resolve leave or accommodation issues
steps.detail: Run the interactive process (LV-02), defer the PIP until 30 days after return from leave, or change the reviewer if the manager is the subject of a complaint; then re-baseline evidence.

steps.label: Draft PIP with SMART goals
steps.detail: Use T-PIP: 3-5 measurable goals tied to role level criteria, interim milestones, support offered, check-in schedule, duration (60 days standard for engineers; 90 for senior or long-cycle roles) and a country-specific consequences statement. Translate for Taiwan and China.

steps.label: Review PIP document
steps.detail: Confirm goals are objective and achievable in the window, the consequences wording fits local law (no at-will language outside the US), and the local-language version controls where required.

steps.label: Deliver PIP meeting
steps.detail: Manager and HRBP meet the employee, explain the gap, goals, support and timeline, and hand over the document. Keep it private and factual; offer EAP information.
steps.control: HRBP attends every PIP delivery meeting.

steps.label: Acknowledge and respond
steps.detail: Employee e-signs receipt (not agreement) and may submit written comments or their own action plan within 3 business days; comments are attached to the file.

steps.label: Provide training or support
steps.detail: Deliver targeted training, a mentor or tooling help. In China this is the statutory training step: record content, hours and attendance; in Taiwan it supports the last-resort showing.

steps.label: Hold weekly documented check-ins
steps.detail: 30-minute weekly check-ins with a written summary to the employee within 1 business day; HRBP joins the mid-point review. Pause the PIP clock for protected leave.

steps.label: Goals met at PIP end?
steps.detail: Manager and HRBP assess each goal against the written measures.

steps.label: Close PIP successfully
steps.detail: Issue a close-out letter confirming success and return to normal check-ins; any recurrence within 6 months restarts at coaching with ER input.

steps.label: Consider reassignment or adjustment
steps.detail: Identify suitable vacancies or job adjustments and document the offer and response. Mandatory before an Art. 40(2) exit in China, expected in Taiwan and good practice everywhere.

steps.label: Exit route approved?
steps.detail: ER and Legal review the full file against the country standard before any termination decision.

steps.label: Hand off to OF-02 or OF-04
steps.detail: Legal approves the exit route and hands the file to OF-02 (involuntary termination) or OF-04 (separation agreement), including union notice in China and the 10-day notification in Taiwan.

raci.activity: Legal review of PIP (non-US and high-risk)

controls.control: ER risk screen completed and documented before any PIP is issued
controls.evidence: ER screen form in case management

controls.control: Legal sign-off on every PIP outside the US and on US PIPs flagged high-risk
controls.evidence: Legal approval in the case file

controls.control: PIP content standard: SMART goals, support, duration, local-language version, approved T-PIP version
controls.evidence: Template version ID in document management

controls.control: Mid-point audit of weekly check-in documentation
Quarterly adverse-impact review of PIP issuance and outcomes by protected group, age 40+, leave and visa status
No termination after a failed PIP without ER + Legal sign-off and, in China, prior union notification (LCL Art. 43)

kpis.name: PIPs preceded by documented coaching
kpis.why: Skipping coaching makes the PIP look like exit paperwork.

kpis.name: PIP success rate (met and retained 6 months later)
kpis.why: A near-zero rate signals PIPs used as a termination formality.

kpis.name: Weekly check-in documentation completeness
kpis.why: Gaps in the record are what lose disputes.

kpis.name: Post-PIP exits challenged (claims, charges, arbitrations)
kpis.why: Measures defensibility of the process by country.

kpis.name: Adverse impact in PIP issuance
kpis.target: No group below four-fifths without documented review
kpis.why: Muldrow-era scrutiny extends to PIP outcomes.

considerations: A PIP is a genuine improvement tool; if the exit decision is already made, use a negotiated separation (OF-04). Sham PIPs damage credibility with courts and with the team.

Timing traps: no PIP right after a complaint, leave request, accommodation request or pregnancy disclosure without ER review; California presumes retaliation within 90 days of certain protected activity.
Pause the PIP clock during protected leave and extend by the leave period; restart with re-baselined expectations after return.
Match the window to the work: a 30-day PIP for an engineer whose deliverable is a 10-week verification milestone is unfair; set interim, measurable outputs instead.

China: training or job adjustment is a statutory step, and renewed failure after adjustment needs fresh, objective evidence; skipping a step converts the exit into unlawful termination (2N or reinstatement).

Canada: poor performance rarely reaches just cause, so the realistic end-state is a without-cause termination with ESA and common-law notice; the PIP buys fairness and protects against bad-faith manner-of-dismissal damages, not notice savings.

India: for non-workers, termination simpliciter on contractual notice is possible if non-stigmatic; for workers, fair process and a documented opportunity to respond are essential, and mutual separation is often the cheaper path.
Most PIPs fail on manager documentation, not on the employee; HRBPs should supply the weekly summary template and review the first two summaries.
Flag visa holders to Immigration at PIP start so any exit handles LCA withdrawal, return transportation and the 60-day grace period correctly.

variations.how: 90-day plan; Dept Head and CHRO involved; Legal often runs a parallel negotiated-exit option.

variations.when: On or returning from protected leave
variations.how: Defer until 30 days after return (LV-03) and re-baseline goals.
Pause, run the interactive process (LV-02) and adjust goals or support as an accommodation before resuming.
Use ER-04 corrective action and, in China/Taiwan, the work-rule-based disciplinary route.
Video check-ins with written summaries; same standards and evidence as on-site staff.
Use only if territory and quota were fair under the CO-04 plan; include pipeline and activity measures, not quota alone.
Report any resulting discharge or termination to the Deputy Labour Commissioner as the exemption conditions require.

countries.us: At-will employment allows termination without a PIP, but a documented plan is the best defense to discrimination and retaliation claims; check comparators and PIP outcomes for adverse impact (Muldrow 2024). Do not count FMLA, ADA or PWFA-protected absences or requests against the employee. Any release at exit for employees 40+ needs OWBPA terms (21 days to consider, 7 to revoke), and Montana requires good cause after probation.
countries.us-ca: Adverse action within 90 days of wage, whistleblower or equal-pay protected activity creates a rebuttable presumption of retaliation (LC 98.6, 1102.5), so ER must clear timing before issue. Keep a human decision-maker and documented rationale where any ADS input is used (CRD regs), hold a timely interactive process if disability or pregnancy surfaces (Gov Code 12940(m),(n)), and have final pay ready at any termination meeting (LC 201, 203).
countries.ca: There is no at-will: poor performance rarely amounts to just cause, which requires clear expectations, warnings, a real chance to improve and a proportionate response (McKinley), and Ontario ESA entitlements are lost only for wilful misconduct. The usual exit after a failed PIP is without cause with ESA plus common-law notice unless an enforceable termination clause applies. Demotion, pay cuts or indefinite suspension during a PIP without consent risk constructive dismissal (Potter 2015 SCC 10).
countries.in: There is no statutory PIP; non-workers can be terminated on contractual notice (termination simpliciter) if the letter is non-stigmatic and not punitive, and the Karnataka Shops Act s.39 requires reasonable cause and 1 month's notice after 6 months' service. For 'workers', follow natural justice (written gaps, opportunity to respond, fair documented process), because poor-performance exits can be challenged before the Industrial Tribunal. Mutual separation is often preferred, and full and final settlement is due within 2 working days of exit.
countries.tw: LSA Art. 11(5) incompetence is a last-resort ground: courts expect objective standards, coaching or training, a genuine improvement plan and consideration of reassignment before dismissal. If termination follows, give Art. 16 notice (10/20/30 days by tenure or pay in lieu), pay severance within 30 days (0.5 month per year, capped at 6 months) and file the 10-day layoff notification with the local authority. Provide PIP documents in Traditional Chinese.
countries.cn: LCL Art. 40(2) requires proven incompetence against objective, communicated standards, then training or job adjustment, then renewed failure; only then 30 days' written notice (or one month's pay in lieu) plus severance N, with the union notified in advance (Art. 43). Missing any step makes the termination unlawful (2N or reinstatement). Employees in Art. 42 protected categories (pregnancy, medical treatment period) cannot be dismissed under Art. 40.

processes.name: Promotion
processes.summary: Moves an employee to a higher job level based on sustained performance at the next level's criteria in the job architecture (PL-03), mainly in the annual cycle alongside CO-02 and off-cycle for genuine scope changes. Covers nomination, calibration, pricing, approval and the downstream checks a level change triggers (exempt status, export access, visa amendments, insider lists). Good looks like explainable decisions against published level criteria, consistent promotion rates across groups and clean, same-day system changes.
processes.trigger: Annual promotion window within the review cycle, or an off-cycle scope change nominated by the manager
outputs: Promotion nomination with evidence against level criteria
Calibrated promotion slate by org
Priced increase and equity refresh recommendation
Job change transaction in Darwinbox
Signed promotion letter or contract amendment
processes.sla: Annual cycle: effective with CO-02 date; off-cycle: 30 days nomination to effective date

steps.label: Nominate for promotion
steps.detail: Submit a nomination in Darwinbox with evidence that the employee already performs at the next level's criteria (scope, complexity, influence), not tenure alone.

steps.label: Validate against level criteria
steps.detail: Check evidence, time-in-level guidelines and peer consistency; run the promotion slate through org calibration and an adverse-impact check before decisions.

steps.label: Price increase and equity
steps.detail: Place pay in the new range (typical 8-12% increase), check pay equity against peers at the new level (CO-06) and recommend an equity refresh under EQ-01 guidelines.

steps.label: Approve promotion?
steps.detail: Dept Head approves within budget; exceptions above guideline need Total Rewards sign-off.

steps.label: Process job change in Darwinbox
steps.detail: Update level, title, pay and manager; the transaction triggers checks for exempt status (MV-05), export re-screen for new technology access (Trade Compliance), H-1B amendment review (MV-06) and insider-list updates (EQ-04).
steps.control: Downstream trigger checklist completed before the effective date.

steps.label: Communicate the promotion
steps.detail: Manager tells the employee first, then the team; issue the promotion letter or contract amendment via e-signature in the local language.

steps.label: Sign promotion letter
steps.detail: Employee signs the letter or amendment; People Ops files it in the personnel record.

steps.label: Give development feedback
steps.detail: Explain which criteria are not yet met, agree 2-3 development actions in PD-01 goals and set a review point.

steps.label: Record outcome for next cycle
steps.detail: Log the decision and development plan so the next cycle starts from documented evidence.

controls.control: Promotion increases within approved guidelines; exceptions need Dept Head + Total Rewards approval
Annual promotion-rate analysis by gender, age 40+, race/ethnicity (US, where lawful), visa status and location
controls.evidence: HR Analytics report reviewed by CHRO

controls.control: Downstream checklist (exempt status, export access, visa amendment, insider list) completed before effective date

kpis.name: Promotion rate by level and function
kpis.why: Too low drives attrition; too high inflates levels.

kpis.name: Promotion adverse impact ratio
kpis.why: Promotion decisions are adverse-action risk under Muldrow.

kpis.name: Off-cycle nomination to effective date
kpis.why: Slow promotions lose the retention value.

considerations: Publish level criteria so decisions are explainable; with pay transparency laws and employees free to discuss pay, inconsistent promotion pay will surface.
Avoid title-only 'promotions' as retention tools; they break the level structure and the pay equity analysis.

A promotion to manager does not remove overtime coverage in Taiwan, and in India a move into a managerial or supervisory role above INR 18,000 a month can take the employee out of 'worker' status; record the duties change.
Check H-1B holders before the effective date: a material change in duties, SOC code or worksite can require an amended petition and a fresh I-129 Part 6 export attestation.
Equity refreshes for promotions follow the EQ-01 grant calendar; do not promise a grant date or size in the promotion conversation.

variations.how: Requires Dept Head and Total Rewards approval and budget; counteroffer-driven moves go through CO-05.
Assign manager training (L&D) and, in California, 2-hour supervisor harassment training within 6 months.
Comp Committee approval under CO-07; Legal checks Form 8-K Item 5.02 and Section 16 implications (EQ-05).

variations.when: Promotion combined with a country move
variations.how: Run MV-02 or MV-03 first; the promotion takes effect in the host entity.

countries.us: Promotion denials are adverse actions after Muldrow (2024), so document criteria and review outcomes for adverse impact; NYC LL 144 bias audits apply to automated tools used to screen NYC promotion candidates. Recheck FLSA and state exempt status when duties change.
countries.us-ca: Newly promoted supervisors need 2 hours of interactive harassment training within 6 months (Gov Code 12950.1), and promotion pay must satisfy the Equal Pay Act, which from 2026 treats stock and benefits as wages (SB 642). CRD ADS rules cover AI tools used in promotion decisions.
countries.ca: Confirm in the promotion letter that the existing termination clause and equity terms continue; changing core terms without fresh consideration can undermine an enforceable termination clause. Ontario's Pay Equity Act and BC pay transparency reporting (50+ employees, first report by 1 Nov 2026) make promotion pay patterns visible.
countries.in: Update the appointment record (designation, wages) and check whether the new role changes 'worker' status, which affects overtime, retrenchment and standing-order protections. Keep basic plus DA at 50% or more of remuneration after the increase (Code on Wages s.2(y)).
countries.tw: Record the promotion in a written, bilingual contract amendment; it does not remove LSA overtime coverage unless the role is an MOL-designated Art. 84-1 position. Up to 10 days of sick leave a year cannot count against promotion decisions from 2026.
countries.cn: Changes to position and pay need written agreement (LCL Art. 35), so issue a signed amendment. Promotion into senior technical or management roles is the moment to add an eligible non-compete and confidentiality terms (LCL Arts. 23-24).

processes.name: Talent review & succession
processes.summary: An annual talent review that assesses potential, readiness and flight risk after ratings close, names successors for critical roles and sets mitigation for key-person risk, especially in scarce chip-design skills. It rolls up from org reviews to an enterprise succession plan reviewed by the CEO and to CEO and executive succession reviewed by the Board. Good looks like real bench depth for critical roles, retention vehicles in place for key people and a current emergency CEO succession plan.
processes.owner: CHRO (enterprise plan), HRBPs (org reviews), Board Nominating/Governance Committee (CEO succession)
processes.trigger: Annual calendar after PD-02 ratings lock; ad hoc on a critical-role departure, acquisition or reorganization
outputs: Critical-role list with key-person risk ratings
Successor slates (ready now / 1-2 years / 3+ years)
Individual development plans for successors and high-potentials
Enterprise succession plan and Board CEO succession materials
Retention actions for key people
processes.sla: Org reviews complete within 6 weeks of rating lock; Board review annually

steps.label: Launch talent review
steps.detail: Confirm the critical-role list with each Dept Head: chief architects, analog/mixed-signal and DFT leads, foundry/PDK owners, security leads and key-customer FAEs, plus all VP+ roles.

steps.label: Assess potential and flight risk
steps.detail: For each direct report, assess potential against behavioral definitions, readiness, flight risk and impact of loss. Placements are confidential and never shared as '9-box' labels.

steps.label: Prepare talent risk data
steps.detail: Provide attrition risk indicators, unvested equity coverage, single points of knowledge, bench strength by critical role and the demographic spread of high-potential nominations.

steps.label: Calibrate org talent review
steps.detail: Calibrate potential across teams, name successors by readiness and set mitigations for key-person risks: knowledge transfer, pairing, retention grants (CO-05/EQ-01).

steps.label: Consolidate enterprise plan
steps.detail: Roll up critical-role coverage, cross-org moves and development investments; identify roles with no internal successor for external pipelining.

steps.label: Review executive slates
steps.detail: CEO reviews VP+ successor slates and confirms emergency interim designations for each executive role.

steps.label: Review CEO and exec succession
steps.detail: The Board (Nominating/Governance Committee) reviews planned and emergency CEO succession and executive bench annually; materials are confidential and minuted.

steps.label: Launch development actions
steps.detail: Agree individual development plans with successors: stretch projects, rotations, international assignments (MV-02), mentoring.

steps.label: Track actions and bench metrics
steps.detail: Report quarterly on development actions, successor readiness changes and regretted losses in critical roles.

controls.control: Talent-review data restricted to calibrated leaders and HR; potential ratings not reused for RIF selection without re-validation
controls.evidence: Darwinbox role permissions; DS-04 access review

controls.control: Board review of emergency and planned CEO succession at least annually
Demographic review of high-potential and successor nominations before finalization
controls.evidence: HR Analytics summary reviewed by CHRO

kpis.name: Critical roles with a ready-now or 1-2 year successor
kpis.why: Measures real bench depth where loss hurts most.

kpis.name: Regretted attrition of high-potentials and critical-role holders
kpis.why: Shows whether retention actions work.

kpis.name: Critical-role holders with an unvested retention vehicle
kpis.why: Forward-vesting equity is the main retention lever in chip design.

considerations: Treat the 9-box with caution: 'potential' is subjective and prone to affinity and age bias; define it behaviorally, calibrate it, never share box placement with employees and never use it as RIF selection criteria.
Key-person risk in chip design is concrete (a single analog lead, the only engineer who knows the foundry flow); mitigate with documentation and pairing, not just money.
Use forward-vesting RSUs or deferred cash for retention; in California, AB 692 bars repayment-style retention bonuses for agreements from 1 Jan 2026.
Before naming a foreign-national successor to a role with controlled-technology access, confirm with Trade Compliance and Immigration that the person can actually hold the role.
Talent-review notes are discoverable and may be reachable through CCPA, PIPL and (from May 2027) DPDP access requests; write defensible, job-related assessments.

variations.how: Activate the named interim; Legal assesses Form 8-K Item 5.02 filing within 4 business days for covered officers; OF-09 if the cause is death.
Identify acquired key people within 30 days of close and put retention agreements in place.
Fold into the parent org's review to keep assessments comparable and confidential.

countries.us: No statutory requirement, but Board oversight of CEO succession is a core governance expectation and investors ask about it; covered officer departures and appointments need a Form 8-K within 4 business days. Keep potential assessments free of age-coded language ('runway', 'fresh blood') given ADEA exposure.
countries.us-ca: Talent-review records are CCPA personal information, and tools that score potential or flight risk are ADS under CRD rules (bias testing, 4-year records) and ADMT under CCPA from 1 Jan 2027. Retention for successors should vest forward rather than rely on repayment clauses barred by AB 692.
countries.ca: No statutory requirements. BC PIPA gives employees access to their personal information, which can include talent-review notes, so keep them job-related; in Ontario, assessments influenced by age, disability or family status create human rights exposure.
countries.in: No statutory requirements; with attrition in the low-to-mid teens and 60-90 day notice norms in Bengaluru GCCs, retention RSUs and visible career paths for VLSI and verification leads are the main levers. From 13 May 2027, DPDP access and correction rights may reach talent assessments (verify how s.7(i) applies).
countries.tw: Identify successors for roles touching national core key technologies and run knowledge transfer inside Trade Secrets Act 'reasonable protective measures'. Moving a successor into a new role must meet the LSA Art. 10-1 transfer principles.
countries.cn: No statutory rules; talent data sent to US HQ systems needs a PIPL notice and separate consent unless the HR-management exemption genuinely applies. Protect key-person knowledge with confidentiality terms and eligible-only paid non-competes (LCL Arts. 23-24; MOHRSS 2025 Guidelines).

processes.name: Compliance training & policy attestation
processes.summary: Plans, assigns, tracks and evidences mandatory training and annual policy attestations: Code of Conduct certification, insider trading, anti-harassment on each jurisdiction's cadence, export control and deemed exports, data privacy, anti-bribery, security awareness and trade secrets. Assignment is rule-based from Darwinbox attributes (country, state, role, supervisor, insider and export flags) so it stays correct through hires, transfers and promotions. Good looks like 100% Code certification, on-time completion above 98%, export briefings completed before access, and audit-ready evidence for SOX, Nasdaq, RBA and customer audits in every language used.
processes.owner: Ethics & Compliance (program owner), Legal (legal cadence and content), Trade Compliance (export modules), L&D and People Ops (delivery and LMS)
processes.trigger: Annual compliance calendar (Q4 planning, Q1 launch); new hire, promotion into a supervisor role, transfer, or a change to an insider or export flag
outputs: Annual curriculum matrix by role and jurisdiction
LMS assignment rules synced to Darwinbox
Completion and attestation records with content version
Code of Conduct certification results and exception log
Audit Committee and customer/RBA compliance reports
Escalation log for overdue items
processes.sla: New-hire bundle within 30 days of start; annual modules within 30 days of assignment; CA harassment within 6 months of hire or promotion; export briefing before access

steps.label: Set annual training plan
steps.detail: In Q4, build the curriculum matrix: Code of Conduct certification (all), insider trading (all; enhanced for designated insiders), anti-harassment, export control (role-based), data privacy, anti-bribery (sales, FAE, procurement, execs), security awareness and trade secrets. Approve with the compliance committee and report the plan to the Audit Committee.

steps.label: Map legal cadence by country
steps.detail: Maintain the jurisdiction rules table: CA SB 1343 (2h/1h within 6 months, every 2 years), NY and IL annual, CT/DE/ME rules, India POSH at induction and annually, China anti-harassment training, Taiwan harassment and bullying measures, Ontario OHS awareness and AODA, BC orientation.

steps.label: Define export-control modules
steps.detail: Specify Technology Control Plan briefings for export-flagged roles, EAR 744.6 US-person training for staff supporting China-based customers or partners, and annual refreshers with attestation.

steps.label: Build and localize content
steps.detail: Produce short modules (15-25 minutes) with a role-based layer; localize into Traditional Chinese (TW) and Simplified Chinese (CN) and other languages as needed. CA harassment content must be interactive and cover abusive conduct, gender identity/expression and sexual orientation.
steps.control: Legal sign-off and version ID before any module is released.

steps.label: Configure LMS assignment rules
steps.detail: Key rules to Darwinbox attributes (work country/state, job family, supervisor flag, designated-insider flag, export flag, sales/FAE, hire and promotion dates) with a daily HRIS-to-LMS sync; new hires get the bundle on day 1 with a 30-day due date.

steps.label: Complete training and attest
steps.detail: Complete modules and e-sign attestations to the Code of Conduct, insider trading policy and TCP; answer the conflict-of-interest and outside-activity questions in the Code certification.

steps.label: Completed by the due date?
steps.detail: LMS status checked at the due date; automated reminders go out at day -7, 0 and +7.

steps.label: Follow up on overdue items
steps.detail: Manager receives the overdue list at day +7 and confirms a completion date with each employee; employees on leave are paused, not counted overdue.

steps.label: Still overdue at day +30?
steps.detail: Ethics & Compliance reviews the residual overdue list by function and country.

steps.label: Apply escalation consequences
steps.detail: Suspend controlled-technology access (IT) for missing export briefings, block trading pre-clearance for designated insiders, note non-completion in the review and bonus modifier where lawful, and refer persistent cases to ER-04.
steps.control: Access and pre-clearance gating tied to completion status.

steps.label: Review certification exceptions
steps.detail: Route 'yes' answers on conflicts, outside activities or foreign talent programs to ER-06 within 5 business days; refusals to certify go to ER; any executive or director Code waiver goes to the Board with 8-K/website disclosure.

steps.label: Retain completion evidence
steps.detail: Keep timestamped completion, content version and attestation text: CA harassment records 2 years, SB 513 training records in the personnel file, TCP records 5 years (EAR Part 762), and SOX/Nasdaq entity-level control evidence.

steps.label: Report to Audit Committee
steps.detail: Quarterly report on completion by country and function, overdue items, exceptions and hotline themes; the same data supports RBA and customer audit questionnaires.

steps.label: Update content for legal change
steps.detail: Annual content refresh plus event-driven updates (e.g., Taiwan bullying rules from 1 July 2026, new state harassment rules), feeding next year's plan.

raci.activity: LMS assignment rules and HRIS sync

controls.control: Monthly HRIS-to-LMS reconciliation: every active employee holds the modules required by the matrix for their attributes
Annual Code of Conduct certification by all employees and directors with exceptions tracked (Nasdaq 5610 / SOX 406 entity-level control)
Export/TCP briefing completed before provisioning access to controlled technology
controls.evidence: Identity-system gate log and LMS record

controls.control: Designated insiders hold current insider-trading training before pre-clearance is granted
California harassment training cadence met (2h supervisors / 1h non-supervisors within 6 months and every 2 years)
controls.evidence: LMS compliance report; certificates retained 2 years

controls.control: Legal sign-off and version control before any module or attestation text is released
Conflict-of-interest disclosures from the certification routed to ER-06 within 5 business days

kpis.name: Code of Conduct certification
kpis.why: Nasdaq and SOX expect a code with enforcement; gaps undermine investigations.

kpis.name: Annual mandatory training completion within 30 days of due date
kpis.why: Regulators judge a program by whether it reaches everyone.

kpis.name: New-hire compliance bundle completed within 30 days
kpis.why: The riskiest period for policy breaches is early tenure.

kpis.name: Export/TCP briefing completed before access
kpis.why: Access before briefing is itself a control failure in an export audit.

kpis.name: Items overdue more than 30 days
kpis.why: Measures whether escalation actually works.

kpis.name: First-attempt knowledge-check pass rate
kpis.why: Shows comprehension, not just clicks.

considerations: Assign by attributes, never by spreadsheet lists; rules keyed to Darwinbox data keep assignments right after transfers and promotions, and lists fail silently.

Keep annual modules short and add role-based depth where the risk is (export for design and FAE teams, anti-bribery for sales in China and India); regulators look for risk-based training, not course hours.
Make consequences real but lawful: access gating and review consequences work everywhere, but wage deductions as discipline are not acceptable (RBA A4) and are restricted in Taiwan, China and India.
Build the Code certification as a questionnaire (conflicts, outside activities, foreign talent programs, awareness of violations) and treat every 'yes' as a case, not a checkbox.
Set a simple global standard: a short annual anti-harassment refresher for everyone plus the full California course on its 2-year cycle, instead of tracking a dozen cadences by hand.
Include contingent workers with system access in Code, security and export modules through vendor terms (PL-05); interns and visiting researchers are frequent export blind spots.

Insider trading training should use engineering examples: design wins, tape-out results and customer ramps are MNPI, and shadow trading in customers' or suppliers' stock is enforceable (SEC v. Panuwat).
In China, a policy can support Art. 39 discipline only if adopted through democratic procedure and acknowledged by the employee, so the attestation record is legal evidence, not administration.
Keep training content from discouraging external reporting: every module on confidentiality must carry the Rule 21F-17, NLRA and whistleblower carve-outs.

variations.how: Bundle on day 1 due in 30 days (Code, insider trading, security, privacy, harassment per jurisdiction, export if flagged); California harassment within 6 months; Connecticut within 6 months.
California 2-hour supervisor course within 6 months plus manager modules on anti-retaliation and handling complaints.
Enhanced insider-trading module and pre-clearance walkthrough before the first open window.

variations.when: Sales, FAE and procurement; China and India staff
variations.how: Anti-bribery module with gifts and hospitality register, commercial bribery (China AUCL) and PCA s.9 'adequate procedures' content.

variations.when: Export-flagged roles and US persons supporting China
variations.how: TCP briefing with signed acknowledgment before access; EAR 744.6 module; annual refresher.
Code certification and insider-trading training administered by the Corporate Secretary.
60-day integration bundle; legacy training records mapped into the LMS.
Deadlines paused; assigned on return with a 30-day window.

countries.us: Harassment training is state-driven: New York requires annual interactive training, Illinois annual, Connecticut 2 hours within 6 months of hire (3+ employees), Delaware within 1 year (50+) and Maine within 1 year (15+). Annual Code certification and insider trading training support Nasdaq Rule 5610/SOX 406 and the Item 408 insider trading policy disclosure (Exhibit 19). Training and attestations must not impede reporting to the SEC, EEOC, NLRB or OSHA (Rule 21F-17).
countries.us-ca: SB 1343 (Gov Code 12950.1): employers with 5+ employees give supervisors 2 hours and non-supervisors 1 hour of interactive training within 6 months of hire or promotion and every 2 years, covering abusive conduct, gender identity/expression and sexual orientation; temporary staff within 30 days or 100 hours; keep records 2 years. SB 513 (2026) requires training records in the personnel file showing trainer or provider, date, duration, competencies and certification. WVPP training is annual and interactive (LC 6401.9).
countries.ca: Ontario requires OHS awareness training for workers and supervisors, information on the workplace violence and harassment program, and AODA training on the IASR and Human Rights Code for every employee with records kept. BC requires new-worker orientation covering bullying and harassment procedures, and those policies must be reviewed annually. Any Quebec-based remote employee triggers French-language training and a psychological harassment policy.
countries.in: POSH Act s.19 requires regular awareness programmes (run them at induction and annually) and orientation for Internal Committee members; refresh IC terms at year-end. A policy, training and gifts register support the 'adequate procedures' defence to the corporate offence under Prevention of Corruption Act s.9. Karnataka IT-exemption establishments must also run a GRC.
countries.tw: With 30+ employees, sexual harassment prevention measures, complaint procedures and disciplinary rules must be adopted and posted (Gender Equality in Employment Act), and the OSH Act workplace-bullying chapter (from 1 July 2026) adds prevention and complaint duties that also cover remote work. General OSH training for new hires (typically at least 3 hours, more for lab work) is required, and periodic trade-secret training supports 'reasonable protective measures'. Deliver in Traditional Chinese and give national core key technology notices to covered roles.
countries.cn: The Women's Rights Law (2022) Art. 25 requires anti-sexual-harassment rules and training, and commercial-bribery training for sales and FAE teams supports handbook-based discipline. Policies that will be enforced under LCL Art. 39 must go through democratic procedure and be acknowledged by each employee, so keep signed attestations. Work-safety training is mandatory for lab roles (Work Safety Law 2021).

processes.name: Learning programs & tuition assistance
processes.summary: Approves and funds job-related external learning (degrees, certifications, conferences) and internal technical academies, with tax-efficient US tuition assistance under IRC 127 and country-specific rules on whether any repayment or service commitment is lawful. The process protects the company from unenforceable clawbacks (California AB 692) while using lawful service agreements where they exist (China, Taiwan, India). Good looks like fast approvals, accurate tax treatment and learning spend concentrated on scarce semiconductor skills.
processes.trigger: Employee request before enrolling in a program, or a manager-nominated development action from PD-01/PD-05
outputs: Approved learning request with business rationale
Country-specific funding or service agreement where lawful
Reimbursement with correct tax treatment
Training record in the LMS and personnel file
Annual utilization and retention report
processes.sla: Approval decision within 10 business days of request; reimbursement within 15 business days of proof

steps.label: Request program or tuition aid
steps.detail: Submit the request in Darwinbox/LMS before enrolling: program, provider, cost, dates, job relevance and time away from work.

steps.label: Endorse business relevance
steps.detail: Confirm job-relatedness or career-path fit and workload cover. Required training for non-exempt staff is paid working time.

steps.label: Eligible under policy?
steps.detail: Check tenure (e.g., 6 months), good standing, annual cap and whether an internal academy (analog design, DFT, verification methodology) covers the need first.

steps.label: Issue country-specific agreement
steps.detail: Apply the approved template: no repayment terms for California agreements unless an AB 692-compliant standalone transferable-credential tuition agreement; pro-rated repayment agreements elsewhere in the US; service-period agreement in China only for professional technical training with documented cost; Taiwan Art. 15-1 minimum service; reasonable pro-rated bond in India.
steps.control: Only Legal-approved template versions can be issued.

steps.label: Complete course and submit proof
steps.detail: Upload completion certificate or grades and receipts within 60 days of course end.

steps.label: Approve reimbursement
steps.detail: Verify proof, apply caps and record the training in the LMS (trainer or provider, date, duration, competencies for California SB 513).

steps.label: Reimburse and apply tax rules
steps.detail: Pay through payroll: US amounts up to the IRC 127 limit excluded, excess taxable unless it qualifies as a working-condition fringe; other countries per local tax treatment (verify).

steps.label: Notify decision and alternatives
steps.detail: Explain the reason and offer alternatives such as internal academies or a later cycle.

controls.control: California agreements from 1 Jan 2026 carry no repayment clause except an AB 692-compliant standalone transferable-credential tuition agreement
IRC 127 annual cap tracked per employee; excess reported as taxable wages
China service-period agreements only with documented training cost (invoices) for professional technical training
controls.evidence: Training cost file attached to agreement

kpis.name: Approval cycle time
kpis.why: Slow approvals push employees to skip or self-fund.

kpis.name: Reimbursement cycle time
kpis.why: Delays erode the benefit's value.

kpis.name: 12-month retention of participants vs. matched non-participants
kpis.why: Tests whether spend buys retention without clawbacks.

considerations: After AB 692, do not rely on clawbacks in California; pay tuition as incurred and accept some attrition, or use a standalone agreement that fits the transferable-credential exception. AB 1697 would move AB 692's start date to 1 Jan 2027; track it.

IRC 127 needs a separate written plan and nondiscriminatory eligibility; tuition above the cap can still be excluded if it qualifies as job-related education under the working-condition fringe rules (verify per case).
Recovering training costs through payroll deductions is restricted in many places (NY Labor Law 193, IL, WA; India's 50% deduction cap); use a separate repayment agreement and invoice.
Prioritize internal technical academies and vendor EDA/foundry training over general degrees; scarce semiconductor skills are the retention and productivity lever.
Mandatory compliance and safety training (PD-06, HS-03) is never subject to repayment anywhere.

variations.how: Dept Head approval with multi-year budget; annual re-approval tied to satisfactory grades.

variations.when: Foundry or EDA training abroad for China staff
variations.how: Service-period agreement with documented cost under LCL Art. 22; amortize liquidated damages over the service period.
Paid under the IRC 127 plan within the combined annual cap.
Manager approval; travel under the expense policy; export review if presenting technical content.

countries.us: IRC 127 excludes up to $5,250 a year of educational assistance, including student-loan repayment, which OBBBA made permanent with the cap indexed after 2026. Several states restrict recovering training costs through wage deductions (e.g., NY Labor Law 193, IL, WA), so collect any repayment by separate agreement.
countries.us-ca: AB 692 (B&P 16608, LC 926) bars requiring repayment of training costs in agreements from 1 Jan 2026, except narrow standalone transferable-credential tuition agreements, with minimum damages of $5,000 per worker; AB 1697 on the Governor's desk would move the start date to 1 Jan 2027. Training records must be kept in the personnel file (SB 513).
countries.ca: No statute governs tuition assistance; repayment terms should be agreed in writing in advance, pro-rated and reasonable (verify enforceability case by case), and cannot be deducted from wages without written authorization and statutory permission (ON ESA s.13; BC ESA ss.21-22). Tuition paid for the employee's own benefit is generally a taxable benefit (verify CRA position).
countries.in: Training or minimum-service bonds are enforceable only as reasonable liquidated damages tied to actual cost and pro-rated (Contract Act s.74; Vijaya Bank v. Prashant Narnaware, SC 2025), and the agreement should be stamped (Karnataka e-stamp). Recovery from final pay is limited to authorised deductions within the 50% cap (Code on Wages s.18).
countries.tw: A minimum-service clause is valid only in return for employer-funded specialized training or reasonable compensation, for a reasonable period and in writing (LSA Art. 15-1; Enforcement Rules Art. 7-1 to 7-3). Keep training cost records to support any liquidated damages.
countries.cn: A service-period agreement is lawful only for employer-funded special professional technical training with documented cost (LCL Art. 22); liquidated damages are capped at the unamortized training cost and courts weigh actual loss and service completed (SPC Interpretation II Art. 12). Ordinary on-the-job or mandatory training cannot support a service period.

processes.name: Engagement survey & action planning
processes.summary: Runs an annual engagement census and quarterly pulses through a third-party survey platform, with confidentiality thresholds, privacy and labor-law clearance by country, results released only to groups large enough to protect respondents, and 1-3 visible actions per team. Good looks like 80%+ participation, action plans in place within 45 days and employees reporting they saw action on the last survey.
processes.owner: HR Analytics (program), HRBPs (action planning), Legal (privacy and labor review)
processes.trigger: Annual survey calendar (census) and quarterly pulse schedule; ad hoc pulse after a reorganization, RIF or acquisition
outputs: Approved survey instrument and confidentiality rules
Privacy notices and consents by country
Results dashboards for groups at or above the reporting threshold
Team and org action plans in Darwinbox
Executive summary for the CHRO and leadership team
processes.sla: Survey window 2-3 weeks; results released within 10 business days of close; action plans within 45 days

steps.label: Design survey and hierarchy
steps.detail: Set items, driver model and optional demographic questions; load the org hierarchy from Darwinbox; fix confidentiality thresholds (minimum 5 responses, 7 for demographic cuts; no comment attribution).

steps.label: Clear privacy and labor review
steps.detail: Confirm notices and consents (CCPA notice at collection, PIPL separate consent for cross-border transfer, SPDI/DPDP consent in India), vendor DPA and transfer mechanism, and pause or adapt the survey if union organizing is known (NLRA solicitation-of-grievances risk).
steps.control: No launch until DS-06 vendor file and country notices are approved.

steps.label: Brief employee representatives
steps.detail: Brief the China enterprise union (where one exists) and the Taiwan labor-management meeting on purpose, confidentiality and how results will be used; not a consent step, but it builds trust and avoids surprise.

steps.label: Administer confidential survey
steps.detail: Vendor sends unique links, hosts responses in the agreed region, runs the survey in English, Traditional and Simplified Chinese and provides participation tracking at threshold level only.

steps.label: Respond voluntarily
steps.detail: Employees respond during work time (non-exempt time is paid); participation is voluntary and managers must not pressure individuals or ask who responded.

steps.label: Analyze and release results
steps.detail: Release dashboards only for groups at or above threshold, with driver analysis and themed comments; route comments indicating safety threats, harassment or misconduct to ER-01 under the pre-announced protocol.

steps.label: Share results with team
steps.detail: Within 30 days, managers share results, discuss 1-2 priorities with the team and avoid any attempt to identify respondents.

steps.label: Agree and track action plans
steps.detail: Record 1-3 actions per team and org-level themes in Darwinbox; leadership commits to 2-3 company-level actions and communicates them.

steps.label: Measure progress via pulse
steps.detail: Quarterly pulses track the priority items and the 'I have seen action' score; results feed the next census design.

controls.control: Reporting threshold (n >= 5; n >= 7 for demographic filters) enforced in the platform; no raw response data to managers
Vendor DPA, cross-border transfer mechanism and China PIPIA completed before launch
Comments flagged for threats, harassment or misconduct routed to ER-01 within 2 business days under a pre-announced protocol

kpis.name: Participation rate
kpis.why: Low participation makes results unrepresentative.

kpis.name: Teams with an action plan within 45 days
kpis.why: Surveys without action lower engagement.

kpis.name: 'I have seen action on the last survey'
kpis.why: The best predictor of future participation.

considerations: Promise confidentiality, not anonymity, unless the platform truly cannot link responses; say in advance what triggers follow-up (threats of harm, harassment).

Under the NLRA, surveys during union organizing can be an unlawful solicitation of grievances with implied promises; comments criticizing pay or management are protected concerted activity and cannot lead to discipline.
In China the survey platform usually sits outside the HR-management exemption, so collect separate consent for cross-border transfer and run a PIPIA, or host in-country.
Keep demographic questions optional and store them separately; never use them to identify individuals in small teams.
One to three visible actions beat a ten-item plan; share back within 30 days or skip the next pulse.

variations.how: 5-10 items, 1-week window, same thresholds; no demographic cuts below org level.
Short, targeted pulse; Legal checks any litigation hold (ER-09) and WARN communications before release.
Results roll up to the next level; managers get no team view.

countries.us: Non-supervisory employees' survey comments about pay, workload or management are NLRA Section 7 protected, and soliciting grievances while organizing is under way can be an unfair labor practice. Avoid questions about lawful off-duty conduct or political views, which several states protect.
countries.us-ca: Survey responses are CCPA personal information: give a notice at collection with purposes and retention, and handle access and deletion requests. Analytics that infer employee traits may need a CPPA risk assessment (rules effective 1 Jan 2026).
countries.ca: BC PIPA permits employee personal information handling reasonable for managing employment with notice, but a voluntary survey is safer on consent; Ontario has no private-sector employee privacy statute, though intrusion upon seclusion applies. Quebec-based employees need a French-language survey and Law 25 compliance.
countries.in: Until 13 May 2027 the SPDI Rules require written consent for sensitive personal data such as health questions; after that DPDP notice and consent duties apply, and voluntary surveys are best run on consent rather than the s.7(i) employment ground.
countries.tw: Give a PDPA notice at collection and get written consent for any health or other sensitive data. Sharing aggregate results at the quarterly labor-management meeting (LSA Art. 83) is good practice.
countries.cn: Survey processing needs a PIPL notice, and transfer to a US-hosted vendor needs separate consent, a PIPIA and a lawful cross-border pathway. Actions that change rules affecting employees' vital interests must go through democratic procedure (LCL Art. 4).

processes.name: Recognition & service awards
processes.summary: Operates peer and manager spot awards and milestone service awards through a recognition vendor, with country-specific award values, payroll tax reporting of every award and anti-bribery guardrails that keep the program strictly internal. Good looks like broad, timely recognition, zero tax reporting gaps and no awards leaking to customers, officials or contractors.
processes.owner: People Ops (program administration), Total Rewards (design and budget), Payroll (tax), Ethics & Compliance (anti-bribery guardrails)
processes.trigger: Manager or peer nomination, or a service anniversary (5, 10, 15, 20+ years) generated from the Darwinbox hire date
outputs: Award record with value and reason
Vendor fulfilment confirmation
Payroll tax entries for each award
Monthly vendor-to-payroll reconciliation
Recognition coverage report
processes.sla: Spot awards fulfilled within 10 business days; service awards within 30 days of the anniversary

steps.label: Nominate or trigger an award
steps.detail: Manager or peer nominates in the recognition platform with a specific reason; service anniversaries are triggered automatically from Darwinbox hire date (with prior-service rules applied).

steps.label: Validate eligibility and budget
steps.detail: Confirm the recipient is an employee (contractors are recognized via their vendor), the value fits the country award matrix and the org's budget.

steps.label: Above threshold or external link?
steps.detail: Flag awards above the country threshold or with any link to a customer, supplier or government official.

steps.label: Review anti-bribery risk
steps.detail: Confirm the award is internal and not a disguised benefit to a customer, official or their relatives; anything external goes to the gifts and hospitality process instead.

steps.label: Fulfil the award
steps.detail: Vendor delivers points, gift cards or catalog items localized by country; service awards include a tangible item and manager note.

steps.label: Tax and report award value
steps.detail: Load award values from the vendor file each pay cycle and apply local tax treatment; non-discretionary awards are included in the regular rate for non-exempt overtime.
steps.control: Monthly reconciliation of vendor file to payroll entries.

steps.label: Recognize publicly
steps.detail: Present the award in a team forum or all-hands, respecting the employee's preference on public recognition.

raci.activity: Program design and country award matrix

controls.control: Every award (cash, gift card, points, merchandise) reported through payroll; monthly vendor-to-payroll reconciliation
Program restricted to employees; any recognition of customer, supplier or government personnel goes through the gifts and hospitality process
controls.evidence: Program rules and Ethics review log

controls.control: Non-discretionary awards mapped to an earning code included in the non-exempt regular rate

kpis.name: Employees recognized at least once a year
kpis.why: Recognition concentrated on a few people breeds resentment.

kpis.name: Service awards delivered within 30 days of the anniversary
kpis.why: Late milestone awards feel like an afterthought.

kpis.name: Tax reporting exceptions in reconciliation
kpis.why: Unreported awards create payroll tax exposure.

considerations: Gift cards are cash equivalents and always taxable wages in the US; vendors often fail to pass values to payroll, so reconcile monthly.
Keep spot awards genuinely discretionary (no promised criteria), or include them in the regular rate for overtime of non-exempt technicians.
Localize values and formats: festival gifts in Taiwan often run through the Employee Welfare Committee, and India and China teams expect festival recognition; a single US catalog does not travel.
Do not create awards restricted by demographic group; keep eligibility open to all to avoid DEI legal risk.
Recognition feeds are a public forum: moderate for harassment, and do not discipline posts that are protected concerted activity.

variations.how: Tangible award under a written plan (US IRC 274(j) qualified-plan treatment where available); prior service with acquired companies counted per policy.

variations.when: Team awards (e.g., tape-out or first silicon)
variations.how: Equal per-person value, delivered through payroll with local tax; gross-up only under an approved rule.
Handled under the IP policy (POL-48) because China and Taiwan have statutory inventor remuneration rules.

countries.us: Cash and gift-card awards are taxable wages; tangible length-of-service or safety awards can be excluded up to $400, or $1,600 under a qualified written plan (IRC 74(c), 274(j); verify current limits). Non-discretionary awards must be included in the non-exempt regular rate (29 U.S.C. 207(e)).
countries.us-ca: Non-discretionary awards also feed California's regular rate for daily overtime and meal and rest premiums. Recognition data held by the vendor is CCPA personal information covered by the notice at collection.
countries.ca: CRA treats cash and near-cash awards as taxable and allows limited tax-free non-cash gifts and long-service awards within annual limits (verify current thresholds). Vacation pay (4%/6%) is calculated on non-discretionary bonuses, which can capture criteria-based awards.
countries.in: Gifts and awards are perquisites taxed through payroll TDS, with a small gift exemption (verify the limit under the Income-tax Act 2025). Keep a gifts register to support the anti-bribery 'adequate procedures' defence.
countries.tw: Festival gifts and bonuses (Dragon Boat, Mid-Autumn) are market practice and often funded through the Employee Welfare Committee; cash awards are taxable salary income (verify). Label discretionary awards clearly, because regular payments can be treated as 'wages' in severance and pension calculations.
countries.cn: Cash and in-kind awards are subject to IIT withholding through payroll (verify treatment of non-cash items). Commercial-bribery rules (Anti-Unfair Competition Law) mean the program must never extend to customer or partner staff.

processes.name: Stay interviews & listening
processes.summary: Structured stay interviews for critical-role holders and high performers, plus onboarding pulses at day 30 and 90, to surface retention risks early and act on them before a resignation. Themes are aggregated with engagement and exit data, and pay-related risks go through the normal off-cycle process. Good looks like annual stay interviews for all critical-role holders, actions closed within 60 days and lower regretted attrition among those interviewed.
processes.owner: HRBP (program), Managers (conduct interviews), HR Analytics (theme analysis)
processes.trigger: Annual schedule after PD-05 talent review; new-hire milestones (day 30 and 90); post-reorganization or after a key resignation on the team
outputs: Completed T-STAY-INTERVIEW notes (restricted access)
T-ONBOARD-PULSE results for new hires
Individual retention actions with owners
Aggregated theme report by org
