Referrals to CO-05, MV-06 or ER-01 where needed
processes.sla: Stay interview within 30 days of scheduling; follow-up actions within 60 days; onboarding pulse at day 30 and day 90

steps.label: Identify interview population
steps.detail: Select critical-role holders and successors from PD-05, high performers with high flight risk, and new hires due for onboarding pulses.

steps.label: Schedule stay interview
steps.detail: Book 30-45 minutes, separate from review or pay discussions, using T-STAY-INTERVIEW questions (what keeps you, what might pull you away, what would you change).

steps.label: Share motivators and concerns
steps.detail: Employee discusses work, growth, manager support, flexibility and pay perception; participation is voluntary.

steps.label: Record themes and commit actions
steps.detail: Record themes in the restricted Darwinbox field and agree 1-3 actions the manager controls; make no on-the-spot promises about pay, promotion or remote status.

steps.label: Flight risk or pay issue?
steps.detail: HRBP reviews the notes for high flight risk, pay concerns or immigration timing concerns.

steps.label: Assess retention response
steps.detail: Evaluate an off-cycle adjustment or equity refresh through CO-05 with a pay equity check; route green-card timing concerns to Immigration (MV-06).

steps.label: Aggregate themes across org
steps.detail: Combine stay-interview themes with onboarding pulse (T-ONBOARD-PULSE), engagement (EN-01) and exit data (OF-07) at org level; no individual attribution.

steps.label: Follow up within 60 days
steps.detail: Confirm actions were delivered and schedule the next conversation; escalate stalled actions to the Dept Head.

raci.activity: Retention response for flight or pay risk

controls.control: Stay-interview notes held in a restricted field (manager and HRBP only) with guidance to exclude health, family and protected-category information
controls.evidence: Access configuration and quarterly note sample

controls.control: Retention offers arising from stay interviews approved through CO-05 with a pay equity check

kpis.name: Critical-role holders with an annual stay interview
kpis.why: Coverage where losses hurt most.

kpis.name: Regretted attrition: interviewed vs. not interviewed
kpis.why: Shows whether the conversations change outcomes.

kpis.name: Onboarding pulse response rate
kpis.why: Early signals only help if people answer.

kpis.name: Actions closed within 60 days
kpis.why: Unkept commitments do more harm than no interview.

considerations: A stay interview must not become a negotiation; managers who promise pay or promotions create inequity and, in Canada and China, possible contractual commitments.
Train managers not to probe family plans, health or immigration status; if the employee raises them, listen and route to the right process (LV-02, MV-06).
Green-card timing is one of the strongest retention levers for Indian and Chinese engineers in the US; route those concerns to Immigration quickly.
Onboarding pulses at day 30 and 90 catch manager and role-fit issues early; route any safety or harassment comment to ER-01 immediately.

variations.how: T-ONBOARD-PULSE at day 30 and 90 in place of a full stay interview; HRBP follows up on low scores.
Stay interviews with key remaining talent within 30 days; coordinate messaging with Legal.
Skip-level listening sessions or focus groups facilitated by the HRBP.

countries.us: Keep conversations away from protected characteristics and respect NLRA-protected discussion of pay and conditions; never tie benefits to staying out of union activity. Notes are discoverable in later disputes.
countries.us-ca: Notes are personnel records and CCPA personal information subject to access requests, and employees may lawfully disclose and discuss wages (LC 232), so do not discourage pay conversations.
countries.ca: A commitment made in a stay interview (promotion, remote status, pay) can become a term of employment or support a constructive dismissal claim if withdrawn, so managers should record actions, not promises.
countries.in: With 60-90 day notice norms and counter-offer culture in Bengaluru GCCs, schedule stay interviews for key VLSI and verification engineers one to two quarters before the increment cycle.
countries.tw: Benchmark concerns against TSMC and MediaTek profit-sharing bonuses and do not record sick-leave use as a retention issue, given the 2026 sick-leave protection rules.
countries.cn: Stay-interview notes are PIPL personal information and should stay in-country or be covered by cross-border consent; any agreed change to role, pay or location must be put in writing (LCL Art. 35).

processes.name: Internal transfer & job change
processes.summary: Moves an employee to a different role, team or manager within the same employing entity and country, whether employee-applied through internal postings or manager-initiated. It bundles the checks a job change triggers: pay and level, exempt status, export-control re-screening, visa amendments, access clean-up and local consent rules. Good looks like fast, fair internal moves with no employee starting a new role before export and immigration checks are complete.
processes.trigger: Employee applies to an internal posting, or a manager proposes a reassignment or team change
outputs: Internal selection record (Greenhouse)
Approved transfer terms (level, pay, release date)
Export re-screen result and TCP briefing if needed
Immigration amendment filing where required
Job change transaction in Darwinbox and signed transfer letter
processes.sla: Selection to effective date within 30 days; sending manager release no later than 60 days

steps.label: Apply for internal role
steps.detail: Apply through the internal job board in Greenhouse and tell the current manager when invited to interview, per policy; manager-initiated moves start at step 2.

steps.label: Select and propose the move
steps.detail: Receiving manager uses the structured interview process (TA-03) and proposes terms with the HRBP; document the business reason for any manager-initiated reassignment.

steps.label: Check level, pay and terms
steps.detail: Map level and pay against the job architecture, agree a release date with the sending manager (maximum 60 days), and flag exempt-status or work-location changes (MV-05, MV-04).

steps.label: Re-screen export access
steps.detail: Check whether the new project involves different controlled technology or source code; confirm license coverage for foreign-person employees and deliver any new TCP briefing before access.
steps.control: No access to the new project's controlled technology until clearance is recorded.

steps.label: Visa impact?
steps.detail: Review whether the change in duties, worksite, hours or pay affects work authorization.

steps.label: File amendment or new permit
steps.detail: Prepare a new LCA and amended H-1B petition (with fresh I-129 Part 6 attestation) for material changes, or update the Canadian, Taiwanese or Chinese permit; the move waits for filing or approval as counsel advises.

steps.label: Process transfer in Darwinbox
steps.detail: Update job, manager, cost center and location; the change triggers LMS reassignment, insider-list review and an access change ticket to remove prior-role access within 5 business days.

steps.label: Sign transfer letter
steps.detail: Employee e-signs the transfer letter or contract amendment in the local language; People Ops files it.

controls.control: Transfer cannot take effect until export re-screen and any required immigration filing are complete
Prior-role system access removed within 5 business days of the effective date
Written consent or contract amendment obtained where local law requires (China, Taiwan, Canada)

kpis.name: Internal fill rate
kpis.why: Internal mobility is the cheapest retention tool.

kpis.name: Selection to effective date
kpis.why: Long releases kill internal mobility.

kpis.name: Access clean-up within 5 business days
kpis.why: Leftover access is a SOX and trade-secret risk.

considerations: Since Muldrow (2024), lateral transfers can support discrimination claims with 'some harm', so document legitimate reasons for manager-initiated moves.
Cap sending-manager holds at 60 days; managers who block moves lose talent to competitors instead.
Transfers are a classic export-control gap: a new project can involve a different ECCN, and foreign-person licenses are often project-specific.
Access accumulation across moves creates segregation-of-duties conflicts and insider risk; remove old access, don't just add new.

variations.how: Run under PL-04; in China and Taiwan get consent or meet statutory transfer principles; in Canada assess constructive dismissal risk.
Add ON-05 relocation support and MV-04 location rules.

variations.when: Transfer to another country or legal entity
variations.how: Use MV-02 (assignment) or MV-03 (permanent transfer) instead.

countries.us: Document legitimate business reasons for involuntary transfers (Muldrow v. St. Louis, 2024) and recheck exempt status and state payroll if the work state changes. H-1B workers generally need a new LCA and amended petition before starting a materially changed role or a worksite outside the LCA's area.
countries.us-ca: A change to exempt status must meet CA's $70,304 (2026) salary floor and duties test, or $58.85/hr for computer professionals, and non-exempt employees must get written notice of wage changes within 7 days (LC 2810.5). New supervisors need 2-hour harassment training within 6 months.
countries.ca: A unilateral material change to duties, pay, reporting line or location can be constructive dismissal (Potter 2015 SCC 10), so get written consent with consideration or give working notice. Employer- or occupation-specific work permits may need changes before the move.
countries.in: Reasonable transfer clauses in appointment letters are generally enforced, but a move to another entity or state needs a new appointment letter and PF/ESI updates. For 'workers', changes to certain conditions of service require prior notice of change under the IR Code (verify the notice period).
countries.tw: Transfers must meet the five LSA Art. 10-1 principles: genuine business need, no worse wages and terms, suited to the employee's ability, help with any location change and consideration of family life. Record the change in a signed bilingual amendment.
countries.cn: Changes to position, pay or location need written agreement unless the contract reasonably permits them and the change is fair (LCL Art. 35); a Shanghai-Shenzhen move needs consent and new social insurance and housing fund registration in the new city.

processes.name: International assignment
processes.summary: Sends an employee to work in another country for a defined period while keeping home employment: business-traveler checks, short-term (3-12 months), long-term (1-3+ years) and commuter assignments. The process gates every assignment on three approvals (host work authorization, export-control clearance, signed assignment terms) and manages tax equalization, shadow payroll, social security coverage, permanent-establishment risk, security briefings and repatriation. Good looks like zero status lapses or payroll penalties, accurate cost estimates and assignees who stay after they return.
processes.owner: Mobility (process), Finance/Tax (tax and PE), Immigration and Trade Compliance (gates), Payroll (home, host and shadow payroll)
processes.trigger: Manager request for cross-border work beyond a routine business trip (policy: over 30 days in a country in a year, or any hands-on work, requires Mobility intake)
outputs: Assignment classification and approved cost estimate
Tax/PE assessment memo and export-control clearance or license
Host work authorization
Assignment letter plus host contract or secondment agreement where required
Home, host and shadow payroll set-up with certificates of coverage
Repatriation or localization plan
processes.sla: Business-traveler assessment 5 business days before travel; short-term assignment 6-8 weeks request to start; long-term 10-16 weeks (visa-dependent)

steps.label: Request assignment with business case
steps.detail: Submit purpose, host country and site, duration, candidate and budget owner through Mobility intake; routine trips under 30 days with no hands-on work get a lighter pre-travel assessment.

steps.label: Classify assignment type
steps.detail: Classify as business travel, short-term, long-term or commuter; select the policy tier and whether home employment continues with a host secondment or a host local contract is needed.

steps.label: Assess tax and PE risk
steps.detail: Tax reviews host income-tax exposure (183-day and treaty tests), dependent-agent or service PE risk from the assignee's activities in China, Taiwan or India, and the intercompany recharge.
steps.control: Tax memo required for assignments over 90 days or involving customer negotiation authority.

steps.label: Export clearance for host?
steps.detail: Check what controlled technology the assignee will access or carry, deemed-reexport licensing for third-country nationals, and EAR 744.6 limits on US persons supporting advanced-node Chinese fabs.

steps.label: Obtain license or restrict scope
steps.detail: Apply for a license or restrict duties, data and device content; brief the assignee on what they may not do, share or carry.

steps.label: Obtain host work authorization
steps.detail: China work permit, Z visa and residence permit; Taiwan WDA permit or Gold Card plus ARC; India Employment visa and FRRO registration; Canada ICT or CUSMA permit; US L-1, H-1B or O-1 for inbound. No productive work on business visitor status.
steps.control: No assignment start without approved work authorization.

steps.label: Build cost estimate and package
steps.detail: Estimate full cost (allowances, housing, schooling, home leave, tax equalization gross-ups, vendor fees) and agree the package tier with the budget owner.

steps.label: Issue assignment letter
steps.detail: Assignment letter under home employment plus a host contract or secondment agreement where the permit requires; state duration, package, tax equalization, limits on signing authority and repatriation terms.

steps.label: Accept terms and complete briefings
steps.detail: Sign documents and complete pre-departure briefings: travel security (HS-02), China device and counter-espionage guidance, TCP obligations, host-country conduct and family support.

steps.label: Set up home, host and shadow payroll
steps.detail: Set up split or shadow payroll by the first host pay period, hypothetical tax deductions, social security coverage (certificate of coverage where an agreement exists) and equity-vesting sourcing feeds.
steps.control: Monthly reconciliation of assignee compensation, including equity, to each jurisdiction.

steps.label: Track days and compliance
steps.detail: Monitor in-country days, permit expiries (120-day alerts), PE-relevant activities and assignment end dates; re-run export checks on project changes.

steps.label: Extend, localize or repatriate?
steps.detail: Decide 6 months before the end date with Mobility and the HRBP.

steps.label: Hand off to MV-03 localization
steps.detail: Transfer the case to MV-03 with a plan to phase out assignment allowances.

steps.label: Plan repatriation and return role
steps.detail: Confirm the home role, return move, host deregistration (permits, residence registration, social insurance) and the final tax-equalization timeline.

steps.label: Close host payroll and true-up tax
steps.detail: Close host payroll, file host returns via the tax vendor, complete the tax-equalization settlement and source trailing equity vests correctly.

steps.label: Return and debrief
steps.detail: Assignee returns to the agreed role, shares knowledge and has a 90-day check-in with the HRBP.

raci.activity: Package, assignment letter and host contract
Home, host and shadow payroll; social security

controls.control: 'Three green lights': no assignment starts until work authorization, export clearance and signed assignment terms are all in place
Tax and PE review for assignments to China, Taiwan or India over 90 days or with customer negotiation authority
Shadow payroll live by the first host pay period; monthly reconciliation including equity vests
Business-traveler day counting with alerts at 90 and 150 days in a host country
Certificate of coverage obtained before start where a social security agreement exists (e.g., US-Canada)
Permit expiry alerts at 120 days with owner assigned
Export re-screen at extension and on any project change

kpis.name: Assignments started with all approvals in place
kpis.why: Starting early creates immigration, export and tax violations at once.

kpis.name: Cost estimate accuracy
kpis.why: Assignments are expensive; bad estimates erode business support.

kpis.name: Payroll, filing or immigration penalties
kpis.why: Direct measure of compliance quality.

kpis.name: Assignee retention 12 months after return
kpis.why: Assignees without a return plan often leave, wasting the investment.

kpis.name: Business trips with a completed pre-travel assessment
kpis.why: Unmanaged 'long business trips' are where most exposure sits.

considerations: Most failures come from extended business trips that are really assignments; enforce the rule that more than 30 days in a country in a year, or any hands-on work, requires Mobility intake.
Use tax equalization for long-term assignees; it keeps them whole, makes equity sourcing manageable and avoids assignees shopping for tax outcomes.
Equity is the hardest payroll item: RSUs vesting during or after an assignment are sourced across countries by workdays, so feed travel days and vest data from the equity platform to the tax vendor.

Social security: the US-Canada agreement allows certificates of coverage, but there is no US-India or US-China agreement, so contributions can be due in both countries, and no US-Taiwan agreement is in force (verify).
Assignees who negotiate or conclude customer contracts, or FAEs acting for the US parent, can create a permanent establishment; limit signing authority in the assignment letter.
Export control follows the person and the data: a release to a third-country national abroad is a deemed reexport, and US persons supporting advanced-node fabs in China need an EAR 744.6 review.
Security matters for China and Taiwan: clean devices, no controlled data on laptops, counter-espionage briefings, and travel approvals for Taiwan staff on core key technology projects.
Family issues sink assignments: check spouse work rights (Canada's spousal open work permit limits since Jan 2025) and schooling before offering.
Start repatriation planning 6 months before the end date; a guaranteed return role is the best retention tool.

variations.how: Pre-travel assessment for visa, tax, PE and export; business visitor status only; no hands-on engineering or customer contract signing.
Home employment and payroll, host work permit, tax protection or equalization, certificate of coverage where available, limited allowances.
Full package with family support, host contract or secondment agreement, tax equalization, shadow payroll and home-leave trips.

variations.when: Commuter or rotator (e.g., Hsinchu to San Jose monthly)
variations.how: Day-count monitoring in both countries, dual payroll exposure and work authorization for each entry.
Deemed-export license or clearance before access; L-1, H-1B or O-1 with accurate I-129 Part 6 attestation.

variations.when: US person assigned to support customers or partners in China
variations.how: Pre-assignment EAR 744.6 review and restricted duties agreed with Trade Compliance.

variations.when: US employee on a short Canadian trip
variations.how: Regulation 102 waiver or Non-Resident Employer Certification; CUSMA or business visitor status as appropriate.

countries.us: US citizens and green-card holders remain taxable on worldwide income while abroad (foreign earned income exclusion or credits may apply; verify per case), and FICA generally continues for US-employer assignees, with US-Canada certificates of coverage available but no US-India or US-China totalization agreement and none in force with Taiwan (verify). Inbound assignees need L-1, H-1B or O-1 status with an accurate I-129 Part 6 export certification, and deemed-export licensing must be cleared before access. US persons assigned to support advanced-node fabs in China need an EAR 744.6 review.
countries.us-ca: California-based assignees may remain California tax residents depending on their ties and assignment length (verify with the tax provider). Assignment or relocation repayment clauses in agreements from 1 Jan 2026 are generally unenforceable under AB 692, and reimbursable business expenses abroad remain covered by LC 2802.
countries.ca: Canadian residents assigned abroad stay taxable in Canada unless they sever residency ties, and CPP/EI can continue under the US-Canada agreement with a certificate of coverage; check Canada's agreements for India or China assignments (verify). Inbound intra-company transferees need 1 year of service with a related entity in the last 3 years, and LMIA-exempt offers go through the IRCC Employer Portal with the C$230 fee. US employees on short Canadian trips need Regulation 102 waivers or Non-Resident Employer Certification.
countries.in: Inbound assignees need an Employment (E) visa, generally with salary above USD 25,000 a year, and FRRO registration within 14 days of arrival for stays of 180+ days under the Immigration and Foreigners Act 2025. International workers contribute to EPF on full salary from day one unless they hold a certificate of coverage from an SSA country, and there is no India-US agreement (subject to pending IW litigation). Assignee activity for the US parent can create PE exposure (verify with Tax).
countries.tw: Inbound assignees need a WDA work permit for specialized work (salary threshold about NT$47,971 a month; verify) or an Employment Gold Card, plus an ARC; residents (183+ days) are taxed under the withholding tables and non-residents at a flat 18%. Foreign special professionals may qualify for the 50% exemption on salary above NT$3M for 5 years. Staff on core key technology projects need approval to travel to mainland China, and there is no US-Taiwan totalization agreement in force (verify).
countries.cn: Inbound assignees need a Foreigner's Work Permit (A/B/C tier), Z visa and a residence permit within 30 days of entry before working, and must be enrolled in Chinese social insurance because there is no US-China totalization agreement; the pension account can be refunded on leaving China. Foreign assignees may choose tax-exempt housing, language and children's education allowances (through 31 Dec 2027) or special additional deductions, not both. Brief assignees on Counter-Espionage Law and data-transfer rules before travel.

processes.name: Permanent cross-border transfer
processes.summary: Moves an employee permanently from one country entity to another (localization), either by terminating and rehiring or by an agreed employer substitution, with explicit decisions on service recognition, severance exposure, equity continuity, benefits and immigration. Good looks like no gap in employment or equity, statutory home-country exit steps completed on time, and a written service-recognition position that prevents later severance disputes.
processes.owner: Mobility (process), Legal (structure and documents), Stock Admin (equity continuity), Payroll (home exit and host set-up)
processes.trigger: Business need or employee request for a permanent move, or a decision in MV-02 to localize an assignee
outputs: Transfer structure decision memo
Home-country separation or transfer agreement
Host-country offer with service-recognition clause
Host work authorization
Equity and benefits continuity confirmation
Home exit documents (certificates, final pay) and host hire record
processes.sla: Approval to host start within 90 days (visa-dependent); home exit documents on statutory timelines

steps.label: Request permanent transfer
steps.detail: Receiving manager confirms an approved position in the host entity (PL-02) and the business case; employee-initiated moves are flagged as local hires on local terms.

steps.label: Choose transfer structure
steps.detail: With Legal and Tax, choose terminate-and-rehire or agreed employer substitution, decide service recognition and set the effective date so there is no gap.

steps.label: Draft separation and host offer
steps.detail: Prepare the home separation or tripartite transfer agreement and a host offer with an explicit service-recognition clause; confirm no home severance is triggered unintentionally.
steps.control: Legal approves the service-recognition wording in every host offer.

steps.label: Secure host work authorization
steps.detail: Obtain the host work permit or permanent residence route before the home employment ends; plan dependants' status.

steps.label: Confirm equity continuity
steps.detail: Confirm the plan treats an intra-group move as continuous service, update entity and tax jurisdiction in the equity platform and set up sourcing for vests that straddle the move; register China participants under SAFE Circular 7.

steps.label: Close home and open host payroll
steps.detail: Pay home final entitlements on local deadlines (e.g., CA last day if terminated, India within 2 working days) and set up host payroll, benefits and social insurance from day 1.

steps.label: Rehire in host entity in Darwinbox
steps.detail: Create the host-entity record linked to the original, keep the original hire date as the service date where recognized, and trigger host onboarding (ON-03).

steps.label: Close transfer and relocation
steps.detail: Complete relocation support (ON-05), confirm all documents are signed and close the case.

raci.activity: Home separation and host offer documents

controls.control: Written service-recognition clause in every host offer, approved by Legal
Equity platform updated on the effective date with no forfeiture event triggered
Home-country exit obligations (final pay, certificates, social insurance transfer) completed on statutory timelines

kpis.name: Transfers with no gap in employment, benefits or equity
kpis.why: Gaps create forfeiture and coverage problems.

kpis.name: Approval to host start
kpis.why: Long transfers stall projects and frustrate employees.

kpis.name: Post-transfer disputes over service or severance
kpis.why: Tests the quality of the service-recognition decision.

considerations: Decide and document service recognition deliberately: Canadian courts count prior service with affiliates in reasonable notice, and Taiwan and China severance depends on recognized service.
An intra-group move is normally not a termination under the equity plan, but confirm the plan's service definition and make sure the equity platform does not trigger a forfeiture.
Retirement and social benefits do not travel: address 401(k) distributions, Canadian RRSP/pension, India PF withdrawal or transfer and China pension refunds in the transfer letter.
Never end home employment before host work authorization is approved; a gap can break visa continuity and benefit eligibility.
Localized employees move to host pay ranges; phase out any assignment allowances over 12-24 months with a written schedule.

variations.how: Local hire on host terms with no allowances; relocation support capped by policy.
Phase out allowances, end tax equalization after a final year and convert to host benefits.
Employment by the PRC entity with a work permit, social insurance from day 1 and SAFE Circular 7 registration for equity.

countries.us: Leaving US employment ends US payroll and group benefits and may trigger COBRA (BN-06); a US citizen employed by a foreign affiliate may stop paying FICA unless a 3121(l) agreement applies (verify). Inbound transferees need US work authorization and a new Form I-9 at the US entity.
countries.us-ca: If California employment is terminated and the employee rehired abroad, all wages and accrued vacation are due on the last day (LC 201, 203, 227.3); an agreed employer substitution with no break avoids the dispute. Relocation-repayment clauses in agreements from 1 Jan 2026 are barred by AB 692.
countries.ca: Prior service with affiliates counts toward common-law reasonable notice, so address service recognition expressly; an outbound transfer ends Canadian employment, requires an ROE, and final pay follows provincial deadlines (Ontario: the later of 7 days or the next pay day).
countries.in: Issue a relieving letter and settle full and final dues within 2 working days (Code on Wages s.17(2)); gratuity continuity across group entities is not automatic, so either pay it or document recognition (verify). EPF can be transferred within India or withdrawn on leaving (verify international worker rules).
countries.tw: Issue a service certificate on request (LSA Art. 19) and record any agreed seniority recognition, because seniority drives annual leave (LSA Art. 38) and severance. A transfer that is really an employer-initiated termination may trigger severance unless the new employer recognizes service (verify).
countries.cn: Issue the termination certificate and complete personnel file and social insurance/housing fund transfer or suspension within 15 days; where the employer arranges the move, prior service generally carries over for severance purposes (verify LCL Implementing Regulations Art. 10). Update SAFE Circular 7 registration for equity.

processes.name: Remote work & work-location change
processes.summary: Approves and administers remote or hybrid arrangements and any change in an employee's work location, because the work location, not HQ, drives payroll tax, wage-hour, leave, non-compete, WARN and export-control rules. Cross-border remote work is prohibited by default and allowed only through MV-02 or MV-03 or a short pre-approved workation. Good looks like every location change registered in payroll before the first pay date, remote agreements on file, and no controlled-technology access from unapproved locations.
processes.owner: HRBP (approval process), Payroll (registration), Trade Compliance and IT/Security (location controls)
processes.trigger: Employee request to work remotely or move, manager-proposed hybrid change, return-to-office decision, or a detected location mismatch
outputs: Approved remote/hybrid agreement (revocable, policy-based)
Updated work location in Darwinbox
State/provincial payroll, tax and workers' comp registrations
Export and sanctions location check
Equipment and access configuration record
processes.sla: Decision within 10 business days; payroll registration completed before the first pay date in the new location

steps.label: Request remote or location change
steps.detail: Submit the request in Darwinbox with the full address, start date, duration and reason; requests linked to a disability or pregnancy go to LV-02.

steps.label: Assess role fit
steps.detail: Apply the role eligibility matrix: lab, validation and hardware roles are on-site; confirm collaboration needs and, for non-exempt staff, timekeeping arrangements.

steps.label: What kind of location change?
steps.detail: Classify the change to route the right checks.

steps.label: Screen cross-border request
steps.detail: Default is decline; exceptions need Mobility, Tax and Legal approval. Sanctioned regions are always blocked, and controlled technology cannot be accessed from abroad without a license review.

steps.label: Register payroll and tax
steps.detail: Register withholding, unemployment, PFML and local taxes and workers' comp in the new US state, or provincial payroll items in Canada (EHT, WSIB/WorkSafeBC), before the first pay date.
steps.control: Location change cannot take effect until Payroll confirms registration.

steps.label: Apply local employment rules
steps.detail: Update pay range or geo-pay adjustment, exempt threshold, leave laws, state notices and restrictive covenants for the new location; confirm WARN and FMLA site attribution.

steps.label: Sign remote work agreement
steps.detail: Agreement states it is policy-based and revocable, sets core hours, equipment, expense reimbursement or stipend, security and data rules, and any on-site days.

steps.label: Configure access and equipment
steps.detail: Ship equipment, enforce VPN and geo-IP controls (block sanctioned regions) and restrict controlled-design data to approved secure environments.

steps.label: Update work location record
steps.detail: Confirm the Darwinbox work location, which drives payroll tax, LMS assignments, postings, WARN counts and notices.

raci.activity: Payroll, tax and workers' comp registration

controls.control: Work-location change requires Payroll confirmation of tax, UI and workers' comp registration before the effective date
Quarterly comparison of login geolocation with Darwinbox work location to detect unapproved work abroad
California remote and hybrid expense reimbursement (LC 2802) configured as reimbursement or stipend

kpis.name: Location changes registered before the first pay date
kpis.why: Late registration creates tax penalties and wrong withholding.

kpis.name: Unapproved cross-border remote work cases resolved within 30 days
kpis.why: Each case carries immigration, PE, payroll and export exposure.

kpis.name: Remote agreements on file for remote/hybrid employees
kpis.why: The agreement is the evidence that arrangements are revocable.

considerations: Default policy: no work from another country beyond a short pre-approved workation (e.g., 10 business days a year) and never from sanctioned regions; unapproved remote work abroad creates PE, payroll, immigration and export exposure at once.

The work state, not HQ, governs payroll registration, minimum wage, overtime, leave, final pay, non-competes and WARN counting; hiring or moving someone into a new state without registering is the most common multi-state error.
Decide the geo-pay rule up front (adjust or not on a move) and apply it consistently; pay transparency laws make inconsistencies visible.
In Canada, a remote arrangement written into the contract turns a later return-to-office mandate into a constructive dismissal risk; keep arrangements policy-based and revocable.
Engineers working with controlled design data from home need approved secure environments; home access is still 'release' if a foreign-person household member can see it.

variations.how: Pre-approval checklist (immigration, tax, sanctions, no controlled data), capped days, company device only.
Run the interactive process under LV-02; a general in-office policy is not a reason to refuse.
Add ON-05 relocation support; H-1B holders need Immigration review first (MV-06).
Give reasonable notice; in Canada assess constructive dismissal risk for contractual remote arrangements.

countries.us: Register for withholding, UI, PFML and local taxes in the new work state before the first payroll, buy workers' comp there and give that state's notices; remote employees count toward FMLA and WARN at the site they report to. Apply the new state's minimum wage, exempt thresholds, leave and non-compete rules (void in MN, ND, OK and WY; WA from 30 Jun 2027).
countries.us-ca: Reimburse all necessary remote-work expenses, including a reasonable share of personal phone and internet (LC 2802), and remember that a move into California brings CA exempt thresholds, local minimum wages and B&P 16600 non-compete voidness. Postings for roles that may be filled remotely in CA need a good-faith pay scale (LC 432.3).
countries.ca: Ontario employers with 25+ employees must have a written disconnecting-from-work policy and an electronic monitoring policy, given to employees within 30 days; document hybrid arrangements as policy-based and revocable. A move to Quebec triggers French-language contracts and policies, QPP/QPIP payroll and Law 25.
countries.in: There is no statutory remote-work regime, though the model standing orders under the IR (Central) Rules 2026 address WFH for services; a move to another state changes Shops Act, professional tax and labour welfare fund registrations.
countries.tw: Remote hours must be recorded to the minute, including evening calls with US HQ (LSA Art. 30), because recorded time is presumed working time under the Labor Incident Act; the workplace-bullying rules from 1 July 2026 also cover remote work. A change of work location is a transfer subject to LSA Art. 10-1.
countries.cn: A change of work location needs written agreement unless the contract reasonably allows it (LCL Art. 35), and a move between Shanghai and Shenzhen changes social insurance, housing fund and local minimum wage rules. Monitoring of remote work requires prior notice under PIPL.

processes.name: Status & classification change
processes.summary: Changes an employee's employment status or classification: exempt to non-exempt (and back), full-time to part-time, fixed-term to indefinite, and contractor to employee. Each change gets a documented legal analysis, remediation decision where misclassification is found, and synchronized updates to Darwinbox, payroll, timekeeping and benefits. Good looks like no exempt employee below the applicable threshold, no long-tenured misclassified contractors and changes implemented within one pay period.
processes.owner: Total Rewards (classification analysis), Legal (sign-off and remediation), People Ops and Payroll (implementation)
processes.trigger: Manager or employee request, annual threshold change (e.g., California 1 January increase), classification audit finding, or contractor tenure review (PL-05)
outputs: Classification analysis memo (duties and salary tests)
Legal sign-off and any back-pay remediation decision
Employee notice or contract amendment
Updated FLSA status, FT/PT and benefits eligibility in Darwinbox
Payroll and timekeeping configuration
processes.sla: Analysis within 10 business days; implemented within one pay period of approval

steps.label: Request status change
steps.detail: Manager submits the request with the reason, or Total Rewards opens it from an audit, threshold change or contractor review.

steps.label: Run classification analysis
steps.detail: Apply salary and duties tests for the work location (FLSA, CA, other states; ON/BC hours exemptions; Taiwan Art. 84-1; India worker test) or the contractor tests (DOL, ABC, CRA and common law).

steps.label: Change lawful and clean?
steps.detail: Employment counsel reviews the analysis and whether past treatment creates exposure.

steps.label: Decide back-pay remediation
steps.detail: Under privilege, estimate unpaid overtime or benefits exposure, decide on voluntary remediation and the communication approach.

steps.label: Communicate change to employee
steps.detail: Explain the change as legal compliance, not a demotion; for new non-exempt staff cover timekeeping, overtime approval and meal/rest rules; issue written notices or contract amendments.

steps.label: Update status in Darwinbox
steps.detail: Update FLSA status, FT/PT, contract type and standard hours; trigger benefits eligibility changes (BN-03) and timekeeping enrollment.
steps.control: Status fields changeable only through the approved workflow.

steps.label: Configure pay and timekeeping
steps.detail: Convert salary to an hourly rate where needed, enable overtime and W-2 code TT tracking, adjust benefits deductions; for contractor conversions end vendor payments and complete I-9 and onboarding.

steps.label: Manage hours under new status
steps.detail: Manager approves overtime in advance, prevents off-the-clock work and reviews timecards each period.

raci.activity: HRIS, payroll, timekeeping and benefits updates

controls.control: Annual pre-1 January audit of exempt employees against next year's federal and state thresholds (e.g., CA $72,384 for 2027)
Classification changes require Total Rewards analysis and Legal sign-off; no manager-only changes
Contractor engagements over 6 months reviewed for conversion or termination

kpis.name: Exempt employees below the applicable threshold
kpis.why: Direct wage-hour exposure, amplified by PAGA in California.

kpis.name: Contractors with tenure over 12 months without a classification review
kpis.why: Long tenure is the strongest misclassification signal.

kpis.name: Changes implemented within one pay period of approval
kpis.why: Delays extend the exposure period.

considerations: When reclassifying exempt to non-exempt, set the hourly rate so expected annual earnings including typical overtime are close to the old salary, and position it as compliance, not demotion.
Lab technicians, test operators and new-grad support roles are usually non-exempt; the computer-professional exemption fits software and EDA roles but not hardware design as such.
Contractor conversion does not admit past liability, but decide remediation deliberately; Canadian dependent contractors can claim reasonable notice even without conversion.
Part-time changes affect benefits eligibility (ACA 30-hour rule), leave accruals and possibly equity vesting under plan terms; spell these out in writing.
India's 'worker' status follows the dominant nature of duties, not title or pay, so re-titling does not change classification.

variations.how: Written agreement with pro-rated pay and benefits; check local part-time rules and any equity plan pro-ration.
Background check (TA-05), I-9 or local right-to-work, IP assignment, export screening (TA-06) and a clean start date.
China: open-ended contract after two consecutive fixed terms (SPC Interpretation II Art. 10); Taiwan: conversion if renewals leave gaps of 30 days or less and service exceeds 90 days.
Bulk review each Q4: raise salaries above the new floor or reclassify with notice before 1 January.

countries.us: FLSA exemption needs a salary of at least $684 a week ($35,568 a year; HCE $107,432; computer employees $27.63/hr) plus the duties test, proven by a preponderance of evidence (E.M.D. Sales v. Carrera, 2025), with higher state thresholds in CA, NY, WA and CO. From 2026 the FLSA overtime premium must be tracked for W-2 code TT, and DOL's Feb 2026 proposal would restore the 2021 core-factor contractor test.
countries.us-ca: Exempt status needs at least $70,304 (2026) or $72,384 (2027) plus California's stricter duties tests, or $58.85/hr ($122,573.13/yr in 2026) for computer professionals. Contractor status is judged under the ABC test (Labor Code 2775), and new non-exempt employees need an LC 2810.5 wage notice.
countries.ca: Ontario IT professionals and BC high-technology professionals (ESR s.37.8) are exempt from hours and overtime rules, but technicians and support staff usually are not, so confirm role by role. Long-term 'contractors' who work like employees face CRA CPP/EI assessments and reasonable-notice claims as dependent contractors (Keenan v. Canac Kitchens, 2016 ONCA 79).
countries.in: Anyone not mainly managerial or administrative, or a supervisor earning over INR 18,000 a month, is a 'worker' with double-rate overtime, retrenchment and standing-order protections regardless of title. Fixed-term employees must have parity with permanent staff and gratuity after 1 year.
countries.tw: There is no salary-based exemption: virtually all employees, including engineers and most managers, are covered by LSA hours and overtime unless in an MOL-designated Art. 84-1 role with an approved agreement. Fixed-term renewals with gaps of 30 days or less and combined service over 90 days convert to indefinite-term (LSA Art. 9).
countries.cn: Comprehensive or flexible working-hour systems for FAE, sales or shift roles need local HR bureau approval, otherwise standard overtime rules apply. SPC Interpretation II (Sept 2025) broadens when consecutive fixed-term contracts require an open-ended contract.

processes.name: Immigration maintenance & green cards
processes.summary: Keeps sponsored employees in valid status after hire (extensions, amendments for job or worksite changes, permit renewals, public access files) and runs permanent residence sponsorship (US PERM, I-140 and I-485; Canadian PR support). It also gives Immigration a seat in RIF and job-change decisions, because layoffs now weigh on H-1B and LCA adjudications. Good looks like zero status lapses, amendments filed before changes take effect and a transparent green-card policy that supports retention.
processes.owner: Immigration (program owner), outside immigration counsel (filings), HRBP (sponsorship decisions)
processes.trigger: Status expiry within 180 days, a planned job, pay, hours or worksite change, a green-card eligibility date under policy, or a planned RIF
outputs: Status and expiry register
LCA filings and public access files
Amended or extended petitions and permits
PERM, I-140 and I-485 filings
Immigration impact review for RIFs and job changes
processes.sla: Extension filings at least 90 days before expiry (180-day alert); amendments filed before the change takes effect; PERM filed within 9 months of sponsorship approval

steps.label: Track expiries and change events
steps.detail: The case system receives a daily Darwinbox feed of job, pay, manager and location changes for sponsored employees and raises 180-day expiry alerts.

steps.label: Notify planned job or site change
steps.detail: Managers notify Immigration before any change to duties, worksite (including remote moves), hours or pay for a sponsored employee; the change waits for Immigration's go-ahead.
steps.control: Darwinbox blocks effective-dating a change for a visa holder until Immigration approves.

steps.label: What action is needed?
steps.detail: Immigration and counsel determine whether the event needs an amendment or extension, starts a green-card case or needs no filing.

steps.label: Refresh I-129 Part 6 attestation
steps.detail: Trade Compliance issues a written classification of the role's technology access for the new or extended petition; licenses are aligned with petition timing.

steps.label: File amendment or extension
steps.detail: Counsel certifies the LCA, posts notice at the worksite, builds the public access file and files the petition (premium processing as needed); Canada, Taiwan and China permits are renewed in parallel.

steps.label: Approve green card sponsorship
steps.detail: Apply the published policy (e.g., eligible after 12 months in role with solid performance) and choose PERM, EB-1 or NIW with counsel; the company pays all PERM costs.

steps.label: Run PERM, I-140 and I-485
steps.detail: Prevailing wage request, recruitment, layoff check for the occupation, PERM filing, I-140 and I-485 when the priority date is current; use AC21 extensions beyond the 6-year H-1B limit.

steps.label: Provide documents and maintain status
steps.detail: Employee supplies documents promptly, clears international travel with Immigration and understands the 60-day grace period and job portability rules.

steps.label: Update records and retain files
steps.detail: Update the status register, I-9 reverification dates and public access files (retained per 20 CFR 655.760); feed status data into RIF planning.

raci.activity: Amendments, extensions, LCA and public access file
RIF and job-change immigration impact review

controls.control: Job, pay, location and manager changes for visa holders blocked in Darwinbox until Immigration approves
LCA notice posting and public access file completed and retained; annual file audit
I-129 Part 6 signed only with a written Trade Compliance classification
controls.evidence: Classification memo in the case file

controls.control: RIF selection lists reviewed by Immigration before notices (LCA withdrawal, return transport, PERM layoff test)

kpis.name: Status lapses
kpis.why: A lapse can force an employee to stop working or leave the country.

kpis.name: Amendments filed before the change takes effect
kpis.why: Late amendments create status violations and back-wage exposure.

kpis.name: Sponsorship approval to PERM filing
kpis.why: Delay pushes priority dates back years for India- and China-born engineers.

considerations: Green-card timing is a major retention lever for India- and China-born engineers facing long backlogs; publish objective sponsorship criteria to avoid favoritism and national-origin claims.

Layoffs now affect immigration directly: the Sept 18, 2026 EO tells agencies to weigh past-year and planned layoffs in LCA, petition and visa adjudications, and PERM requires notice to laid-off US workers in the occupation within the prior 6 months (verify); coordinate RIF timing with pending filings.
Remote work moves are the most common amendment miss: a worksite outside the LCA's area needs a new LCA and usually an amended petition before the move (MV-04).
PERM costs must be paid by the employer and cannot be recovered through clawbacks; California's AB 692 also bars repayment terms in new agreements.
On termination of an H-1B worker, withdraw the LCA, notify USCIS and offer return transportation; the worker has up to 60 days' grace to change status or employer.

variations.when: Remote or relocation move for an H-1B worker
variations.how: New LCA and amended petition before the move; post notice at the new worksite.

variations.when: Promotion or role change during a green-card case
variations.how: Counsel assesses whether PERM or I-140 must restart; after I-485 has been pending 180 days, same-or-similar job portability may apply.
Bona fide termination steps, grace-period communication, and PERM and H-1B impact review under the Sept 2026 EO.
Canadian work permits renewed before expiry with PR planning; Taiwan Gold Card or WDA permit and ARC renewals; China work permit and residence permit renewals.

countries.us: Material changes such as a worksite outside the LCA's area need a new LCA and amended H-1B petition, with LCA notice and a public access file (20 CFR 655.760); on termination, withdraw the LCA, notify USCIS and offer return fare, and the worker has a 60-day grace period (8 CFR 214.1(l)(2)). The Sept 18, 2026 EO has agencies weigh layoffs in LCA and petition decisions, and DOL's proposed prevailing-wage increase (Level I-IV to the 34th/52nd/70th/88th percentiles) would raise H-1B and PERM wage floors.
countries.us-ca: No separate state immigration regime, but sponsored employees are covered by the same pay-scale, Equal Pay Act and AB 692 rules, so immigration-cost repayment terms in agreements from 1 Jan 2026 are unenforceable. A remote move within or out of California can still need a new LCA.
countries.ca: Employers of work-permit holders must keep wages and duties consistent with the permit, keep records 6 years and diarize expiries (9-series SINs expire with the permit); PGWPs cannot be extended, so start LMIA or PR planning early. IRCC consulted in Aug-Sep 2026 on an Express Entry category for H-1B holders, a potential recruiting channel for 2027.
countries.in: Foreign nationals on Employment visas must keep FRRO registration current under the Immigration and Foreigners Act 2025 (verify employer reporting duties). India has no employer-sponsored permanent residence route, so the main issue is supporting Indian engineers' US status and green-card timing.
countries.tw: The 2026 Foreign Professionals Act amendments allow faster APRC (1 year for high earners) and work rights for spouses; track WDA work-permit, Gold Card and ARC renewals. PRC nationals are effectively barred from employment in Taiwan.
countries.cn: Renew the Foreigner's Work Permit and residence permit before expiry and update them on job or employer changes; foreign employees' contracts run for at most 5 years. SPC Interpretation II Art. 4 recognizes employment only for foreigners with permanent residence or valid permits.
